```{r setup, include=FALSE}
## Loads every path (DHS folder, data/intermediate, lookups) from config.R,
## and runs every chunk from data/intermediate/, where the pipeline's files live.
source(here::here("config.R"))
source(here::here("R", "check_dhs.R"))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = INTER_DIR)
check_dhs_files()

## Checkpoints: reading the big DHS files is slow, so the first read is saved to
## data/intermediate/checkpoints/. Later runs load the saved copy in seconds. The file
## name includes a fingerprint of the variable list, so adding a variable forces a fresh read.
## Set REBUILD <- TRUE to force every file to be read again from the DHS originals.
REBUILD <- FALSE
checkpoint <- function(name, vars, expr) {
  dir.create(file.path(INTER_DIR, "checkpoints"), showWarnings = FALSE)
  key  <- substr(digest::digest(vars), 1, 8)
  path <- file.path(INTER_DIR, "checkpoints", paste0(name, "_", key, ".rds"))
  if (!REBUILD && file.exists(path)) { message("Loaded checkpoint: ", basename(path)); return(readRDS(path)) }
  out <- expr
  saveRDS(out, path)
  out
}
```


This document runs the full analysis for the thesis, from the raw NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 files to every
table and figure. It replicates the propensity-score-matched difference-in-differences evaluation of
the Aspirational Districts Programme by Agarwal and Mishra (2024, A&M below) and extends it to women's
empowerment. Each stage writes its results to `outputs/tables/` and `outputs/figures/`; intermediate
files go to `data/intermediate/`.

| Stage | Content |
|---|---|
| 01 | NFHS child, household and births data: covariates and health outcomes |
| 02 | Treatment: the 112 Aspirational Districts |
| 03 | Covariates from outside NFHS (SECC 2011, U-DISE 2015-16, Saubhagya) |
| 05 | Linking NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 districts; the estimation sample |
| 06 | Women's empowerment outcomes |
| 07 | Descriptive statistics |
| 08 | Propensity-score matching |
| 09 | ATT difference-in-differences and robustness checks |
| 10 | Index weights from pre-treatment data |
| 11 | Validation of the treatment variable |

# Stage 01: Build the child-level dataset

Reads the NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 children's (KR), household (HR), women's (IR) and births (BR)
files, builds every Table 1/3 covariate and Table 2 outcome for each child, and collapses to
district level. Produces `nfhs_mega_v2.csv`, `district_covariates_baseline.csv` and
`district_outcomes_panel.csv`.

## 1.1 Packages and paths

```{r s01-packages}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(suppressWarnings({ library(haven); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(stringr); library(readr) }))   # hide 'built under R x.y' notices

DHS_DIR <- DHS_RAW_DIR
OUT_DIR <- INTER_DIR
```

## 1.2 Children's file (KR) and district assignment

sdistri (NFHS-4) was validated against the DHS GPS cluster locations and district shapefile, with zero
disagreements. sdist (NFHS-5) is read in the same `read_dta()` call as the other KR variables,
because merging it separately caused many-to-many row inflation. The MCP card question has a
different name in each round (s412 / s413) and is harmonised immediately.

```{r s01-kr}
## Every variable read from the children's (KR) file. Labels are DHS's own,
## read from both DTA files. Same variable and meaning in both rounds unless noted.
KR_VARS <- c(
  ## -- Identifiers and survey design
  "v001",   # cluster number
  "v002",   # household number
  "v003",   # mother's line number in the household
  "v005",   # sample weight, 6 decimals (NFHS-4: national women's weight; NFHS-5: women's individual weight)
  "v006",   # month of interview
  "v007",   # year of interview
  "v008",   # date of interview, century month code (months since Jan 1900)
  "v024",   # state
  "v025",   # urban or rural
  ## -- Child characteristics
  "b4",     # sex of child
  "b8",     # current age of child, in years
  "b9",     # who the child lives with
  "bidx",   # birth order position (1 = most recent birth)
  "b3",     # child's date of birth, century month code
  ## -- Anthropometry (Table 2 outcomes)
  "hw70",   # height-for-age z-score x100 (stunting)
  "hw72",   # weight-for-height z-score x100 (wasting)
  "hw71",   # weight-for-age z-score x100 (underweight)
  ## -- Breastfeeding, illness and treatment (Table 2 outcomes)
  "m34",    # when the child was first put to the breast
  "h11",    # had diarrhoea recently (population base for ORS and zinc)
  "h13",    # given oral rehydration (ORS)
  "h15e",   # given zinc
  "h22",    # had fever in the last two weeks (population base for fever treatment)
  "h46a",   # where treatment for fever was first sought (first place only; kept for reference)
  "h31",    # had cough in the last two weeks
  "h31b",   # short, rapid breaths
  "h31c",   # problem in the chest or blocked/running nose
  ## h32a-h32x: fever/cough, each place advice or treatment was sought (1 = yes).
  ## The letters mean different places in the two rounds; see section 1.8.
  paste0("h32", letters[1:24]),
  ## -- Age, used to define the MAD population (children 6-23 months)
  "hw1",    # child's age in months, height/weight section (NFHS-4's age variable here)
  "b19",    # child's current age in months (NFHS-5 only; not in the NFHS-4 file)
  ## -- Breastfeeding status and meal frequency (MAD)
  "m4",     # duration of breastfeeding (95 = still breastfeeding)
  "m39",    # times the child ate solid, semi-solid or soft food yesterday
  ## -- Foods given yesterday (MDD food groups)
  "v411",   # gave child tinned, powdered or fresh milk
  "v411a",  # gave child baby formula
  "v412a",  # gave child fortified baby food (Cerelac etc.)
  "v414a",  # gave child chicken, duck or other birds
  "v414e",  # gave child bread, noodles, other grain foods
  "v414f",  # gave child potatoes, cassava, other tubers
  "v414g",  # gave child eggs
  "v414i",  # gave child pumpkin, carrots, squash (yellow/orange inside)
  "v414j",  # gave child dark green leafy vegetables
  "v414k",  # gave child mangoes, papayas, other vitamin A fruits
  "v414l",  # gave child any other fruits
  "v414m",  # gave child liver, heart, other organs
  "v414n",  # gave child fish or shellfish
  "v414o",  # gave child beans, peas, lentils, nuts
  "v414p",  # gave child cheese, yogurt, other milk products
  "v414t",  # gave child any other meat
  "v414v",  # gave child yogurt
  ## -- Milk feeds, for meal frequency of non-breastfed children (MAD)
  "v469e",  # times gave child powdered/tinned/fresh milk
  "v469f",  # times gave child infant formula
  "v469x",  # times gave child yogurt
  ## -- Antenatal care and delivery for this child's birth, and mother's education.
  ##    Read from the children's file, so each child carries the record for its own birth.
  "m1",     # number of tetanus injections before birth
  "m13",    # timing of first antenatal check (months of pregnancy)
  "m14",    # number of antenatal visits during pregnancy
  "m15",    # place of delivery
  "m45",    # during pregnancy, given or bought iron tablets/syrup
  "m46",    # days iron tablets or syrup taken
  "v106",   # mother's highest educational level
  "v133",   # mother's education in single years
  ## -- Remaining Table 2 outcomes
  "midx",   # index to maternity history (1 = mother's most recent birth)
  "b5",     # child is alive
  "m3a",    # assistance at delivery: doctor
  "m3b",    # assistance at delivery: ANM/nurse/midwife/LHV
  "m3c",    # assistance at delivery: other health personnel
  "h1",     # has health card (1 = yes, seen)
  "h2",     # received BCG      (1 = date on card, 2 = reported by mother, 3 = marked on card)
  "h3", "h5", "h7",     # received DPT 1, 2, 3
  "h51", "h52", "h53",  # received pentavalent 1, 2, 3 (NFHS-5; replaces DPT)
  "h4", "h6", "h8",     # received polio 1, 2, 3 (polio 0 at birth, h0, is not counted)
  "h9"      # received measles / first measles-containing vaccine (NFHS-5 adds 4 = vaccination identified)
)

kr4 <- checkpoint("kr4", KR_VARS, read_dta(dhs_file("IAKR74FL.DTA"),
                col_select = any_of(c(KR_VARS, "sdistri", "s412"))) %>%
  zap_labels() %>%
  mutate(distcode = as.numeric(sdistri), survey_round = "nfhs4", post = 0L,
         mcp_card_raw = s412) %>%
  select(-sdistri, -s412))

cat("NFHS-4 KR rows:", nrow(kr4), "| districts:", n_distinct(kr4$distcode), "\n")

kr5 <- checkpoint("kr5", KR_VARS, read_dta(dhs_file("IAKR7EFL.DTA"),
                col_select = any_of(c(KR_VARS, "sdist", "s413"))) %>%
  zap_labels() %>%
  mutate(distcode = as.numeric(sdist), survey_round = "nfhs5", post = 1L,
         mcp_card_raw = s413) %>%
  select(-sdist, -s413))

cat("NFHS-5 KR rows:", nrow(kr5), "| districts:", n_distinct(kr5$distcode), "\n")

## Check: any_of() silently skips variables that are not in the file. Expected gaps: b19 and
## h51-h53 (pentavalent) are not in NFHS-4. Anything else listed here is a problem.
## Stored now, because later sections rename some of these variables.
kr4_missing <- setdiff(KR_VARS, names(kr4))
kr5_missing <- setdiff(KR_VARS, names(kr5))
cat("Missing from NFHS-4 KR:", kr4_missing, "\n")
cat("Missing from NFHS-5 KR:", kr5_missing, "\n")
```

## 1.3 Household file (HR): water, toilet, electricity

The household file supplies three baseline (Table 1/3) covariates: access to drinking water,
individual toilets, and electricity. It is joined to children later on cluster (`v001`) and
household number (`v002`). `hv225` is read alongside `hv205` because "individual toilet" means an
improved facility that is **not shared** with other households, not just an improved one.

```{r s01-hr}
## Every variable read from the household (HR) file. Labels are DHS's own,
## read from both DTA files; identical in both rounds.
HR_VARS <- c(
  "hv201",  # source of drinking water
  "hv205",  # type of toilet facility
  "hv225",  # toilet shared with other households
  "hv206",  # has electricity
  "hv009"   # number of household members
)

## Also read for the household-level covariates in section 1.7:
##   hv005 household sample weight (6 decimals), hv012 number of de jure members,
##   hv015 result of household interview, and the district code
##   (shdistri in NFHS-4, shdist in NFHS-5; renamed hh_distcode).
## hv001/hv002 are renamed to v001/v002 so they match the children's file.
read_hr <- function(path, distvar) {
  read_dta(path, col_select = any_of(c("hv001", "hv002", "hv005", "hv012", "hv015",
                                       distvar, HR_VARS))) %>%
    zap_labels() %>%
    rename(v001 = hv001, v002 = hv002, hh_distcode = all_of(distvar)) %>%
    mutate(hh_distcode = as.numeric(hh_distcode))
}

hr4 <- checkpoint("hr4", HR_VARS, read_hr(dhs_file("IAHR74FL.DTA"), "shdistri"))
hr5 <- checkpoint("hr5", HR_VARS, read_hr(dhs_file("IAHR7EFL.DTA"), "shdist"))

## Check 1: one row per household. A duplicate (v001, v002) pair would copy
## children when HR is joined to KR, inflating the sample. Both should say FALSE.
cat("NFHS-4 HR rows:", nrow(hr4), "| duplicate households?",
    any(duplicated(hr4[, c("v001", "v002")])), "\n")
cat("NFHS-5 HR rows:", nrow(hr5), "| duplicate households?",
    any(duplicated(hr5[, c("v001", "v002")])), "\n")

## Check 2: same silent-skip check as for KR. Nothing should be missing.
cat("Missing from NFHS-4 HR:", setdiff(HR_VARS, names(hr4)), "\n")
cat("Missing from NFHS-5 HR:", setdiff(HR_VARS, names(hr5)), "\n")
```

## 1.4 Antenatal care and delivery variables: readable names

These six variables now come straight from the children's file, so each child carries the record
for **its own** birth by construction. They are renamed to the names every later stage uses, so
nothing downstream changes. `iron_given` is kept for reference only; the full-ANC rule uses
`ifa_days`.

```{r s01-anc-rename}
ANC_NAMES <- c(
  anc_timing_months = "m13",   # timing of first ANC check (months)
  anc_visits        = "m14",   # number of ANC visits
  delivery_place    = "m15",   # place of delivery
  tetanus_doses     = "m1",    # tetanus injections before birth
  iron_given        = "m45",   # given/bought iron tablets (reference only)
  ifa_days          = "m46"    # days of iron/folic acid taken (needed for full ANC)
)

kr4 <- kr4 %>% rename(all_of(ANC_NAMES))
kr5 <- kr5 %>% rename(all_of(ANC_NAMES))

## Quick look: how many children have an ANC-visit record in each round. ANC
## questions are asked about the most recent birth, so older siblings are NA.
cat("NFHS-4 children with anc_visits recorded:", sum(!is.na(kr4$anc_visits)), "of", nrow(kr4), "\n")
cat("NFHS-5 children with anc_visits recorded:", sum(!is.na(kr5$anc_visits)), "of", nrow(kr5), "\n")
```

## 1.5 Join the household file and stack the two rounds

Each child gets its household's water, toilet and electricity variables (joined on cluster and
household number). The join must not add or drop children, so the row count is checked.

`v005` is the DHS sample weight multiplied by 1,000,000; it is divided back down before use.

```{r s01-join-stack}
join_hr <- function(kr, hr, round_label) {
  merged <- kr %>% left_join(hr %>% select(v001, v002, all_of(HR_VARS)), by = c("v001", "v002"))
  cat(round_label, "| children before:", nrow(kr), "| after:", nrow(merged),
      "| unchanged:", nrow(merged) == nrow(kr),
      "| with household record:", sum(!is.na(merged$hv009)), "\n")
  stopifnot(nrow(merged) == nrow(kr))   # stop immediately if the join duplicated children
  merged
}

mega4 <- join_hr(kr4, hr4, "NFHS-4") %>% mutate(weight = v005 / 1e6)
mega5 <- join_hr(kr5, hr5, "NFHS-5") %>% mutate(weight = v005 / 1e6)

nfhs_mega <- bind_rows(mega4, mega5)
cat("Stacked rows:", nrow(nfhs_mega), "\n")
print(table(nfhs_mega$survey_round))
```

## 1.6 Child-level covariates and outcomes: nutrition, antenatal care, delivery

Builds seven indicators, each 0/1 per child. Missing-value codes are DHS's own, read from the
value labels in both rounds' files: 98 = "don't know" for ANC timing and visits, 8 = "don't know"
for tetanus injections and iron tablets, 998 = "don't know" for days of iron taken, and 9996 and
above = implausible or flagged anthropometry.

Three coding rules follow from the questionnaire's skip pattern:

- A mother with no ANC visits counts as 0 for "ANC in first trimester", not missing. Her ANC timing
  is blank because the question was skipped, not because the answer is unknown.
- Children whose ANC-visit number is missing (the question does not apply, for example older
  siblings) are excluded, not set to 0.
- A mother who took no iron tablets (`m45 = 0`) is never asked how many days she took them, so
  `m46` is blank. She counts as 0 days, so she does not meet full ANC. Treating the blank as missing
  would drop 9,981 NFHS-4 and 8,053 NFHS-5 children among mothers with 4+ visits and push full ANC
  upwards.

```{r s01-covariates-health}
nfhs_mega <- nfhs_mega %>%
  mutate(
    ## -- Stunting, wasting, severe wasting (z-scores stored x100) --
    haz             = ifelse(hw70 >= 9996, NA, hw70) / 100,   # height-for-age
    stunted         = as.integer(haz < -2),
    whz             = ifelse(hw72 >= 9996, NA, hw72) / 100,   # weight-for-height (NOT hw71)
    wasted          = as.integer(whz < -2),
    severely_wasted = as.integer(whz < -3),

    ## -- At least 4 ANC visits. 0 is a real answer ("no visits"); 98 = don't know --
    anc_visits_clean = ifelse(anc_visits == 98, NA, anc_visits),
    anc_4plus_visits = as.integer(anc_visits_clean >= 4),

    ## -- First ANC visit in the first trimester (<= 3 months of pregnancy) --
    anc_timing_clean    = ifelse(anc_timing_months == 98, NA, anc_timing_months),
    anc_first_trimester = case_when(
      anc_visits_clean == 0 ~ 0L,                          # no ANC at all -> did not meet it
      TRUE ~ as.integer(anc_timing_clean <= 3)
    ),

    ## -- Full ANC: 4+ visits AND 1+ tetanus injection AND 100+ days of iron/folic acid --
    tetanus_clean  = ifelse(tetanus_doses == 8, NA, tetanus_doses),   # 8 = don't know
    ifa_days_clean = case_when(
      iron_given == 0 ~ 0,                                 # no tablets -> 0 days
      iron_given == 8 ~ NA_real_,                          # don't know whether given
      ifa_days == 998 ~ NA_real_,                          # don't know how many days
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(ifa_days)
    ),
    full_anc = as.integer(anc_visits_clean >= 4 & tetanus_clean >= 1 & ifa_days_clean >= 100),

    ## -- Institutional birth: m15 codes 20-27 public, 30-33 private or NGO facility --
    institutional_birth = as.integer(delivery_place >= 20 & delivery_place <= 33)
  )

## Check: non-missing count and weighted % for each indicator, by round.
nfhs_mega %>%
  group_by(survey_round) %>%
  summarise(across(c(stunted, wasted, severely_wasted, anc_4plus_visits,
                     anc_first_trimester, full_anc, institutional_birth),
                   list(n = ~ sum(!is.na(.)),
                        pct = ~ round(weighted.mean(., weight, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1)))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-survey_round, names_to = c("indicator", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "^(.*)_(n|pct)$") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey_round, values_from = c(n, pct)) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

## 1.7 Household-level covariates: toilet and water

Agarwal & Mishra measure these two covariates as the inverse of two NFHS-4 fact-sheet indicators:
"Percent of population living in households that use an improved sanitation facility" and
"Percent of population living in households with an improved drinking water source". So they are
built here from the household file, one row per household, weighted to represent the
**population** living in households: household weight (`hv005`) times number of de jure members
(`hv012`). Averaging over children instead would count a household once per child under five.

Classification follows the NFHS-4 national report (FR339):

- **Improved sanitation (Table 2.2):** flush or pour-flush to sewer, septic tank or pit latrine;
  VIP/biogas latrine; pit latrine with slab; twin pit/composting toilet; **and not shared** with
  other households. Dry toilets are listed as **unimproved**.
- **Improved drinking water (Table 2.1):** piped, public tap, tube well/borehole, protected well,
  protected spring, rainwater, **and community RO plant**. Bottled water and tanker/cart are
  unimproved.

Three details of the classification:

1. The toilet must be improved **and** not shared, because the NFHS-4 indicator A&M cite is defined
   that way (48.4% of households nationally).
2. Dry toilets (`hv205 = 44`) count as unimproved, as in FR339 Table 2.2.
3. Community RO plants (`hv201 = 72`) count as improved, as in FR339 Table 2.1.

The same NFHS-4 definitions are applied to NFHS-5 so the two rounds are comparable. Note that
NFHS-5's own published figures use the later WHO/UNICEF definitions (which also count tanker
trucks and carts), so NFHS-5 values here will not match the NFHS-5 fact sheet. Only the NFHS-4
values enter the propensity score.

```{r s01-hh-covariates}
build_hh <- function(hr, round_label) {
  hr %>%
    filter(hv015 == 1) %>%                                   # completed household interviews only
    mutate(
      survey_round = round_label,
      hh_weight    = hv005 / 1e6,                            # household weight
      pop_weight   = hh_weight * hv012,                      # population living in the household
      toilet_improved_type = as.integer(hv205 %in% c(11, 12, 13, 21, 22, 41)),
      toilet_improved      = as.integer(toilet_improved_type == 1 & hv225 %in% 0),  # improved AND not shared
      water_improved       = as.integer(hv201 %in% c(11, 12, 13, 14, 21, 31, 41, 51, 72))
    )
}

hh <- bind_rows(build_hh(hr4, "nfhs4"), build_hh(hr5, "nfhs5"))

## Check 1: national NFHS-4 values against FR339.
##   Sanitation: 48.4 (households and de jure population), Table 2.2
##   Water:      89.9 (households), 90.2 (de jure population), Table 2.1
hh %>%
  group_by(survey_round) %>%
  summarise(
    households       = n(),
    sanitation_hh    = round(weighted.mean(toilet_improved, hh_weight)  * 100, 1),
    sanitation_pop   = round(weighted.mean(toilet_improved, pop_weight) * 100, 1),
    water_hh         = round(weighted.mean(water_improved,  hh_weight)  * 100, 1),
    water_pop        = round(weighted.mean(water_improved,  pop_weight) * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  print()

## Check 2: the household file's district codes must be the same set as the
## children's file's, or the two sources would describe different districts.
cat("NFHS-4: KR districts not in HR:", setdiff(unique(kr4$distcode), unique(hr4$hh_distcode)),
    "| HR districts not in KR:", setdiff(unique(hr4$hh_distcode), unique(kr4$distcode)), "\n")
cat("NFHS-5: KR districts not in HR:", setdiff(unique(kr5$distcode), unique(hr5$hh_distcode)),
    "| HR districts not in KR:", setdiff(unique(hr5$hh_distcode), unique(kr5$distcode)), "\n")

## District x round covariates, population-weighted. Joined onto the district panels.
district_hh_covariates <- hh %>%
  group_by(distcode = hh_distcode, survey_round) %>%
  summarise(
    pct_no_individual_toilet = (1 - weighted.mean(toilet_improved, pop_weight)) * 100,
    pct_no_water_access      = (1 - weighted.mean(water_improved,  pop_weight)) * 100,
    n_households             = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("District x round rows:", nrow(district_hh_covariates), "\n")
summary(district_hh_covariates$n_households)
```

## 1.8 Table 2 outcomes: age, underweight, MCP card, breastfeeding, ORS, zinc, fever/ARI

These are Agarwal & Mishra's outcome variables, built for both rounds. Definitions follow A&M's
Table 2 wording and the NFHS reports; every missing-value code below was read from the value
labels in both rounds' files.

**Child age.** Built the DHS way in both rounds: interview date minus birth date, in
months (`v008 - b3`). The chunk also shows how often it disagrees with `hw1` (NFHS-4) and `b19`
(NFHS-5), the two alternative age variables.

**Three definitions that follow A&M's wording and the NFHS reports:**

1. **Breastfed within one hour.** A&M's indicator is "children **under age 3** years
   breastfed within one hour of birth", as in the NFHS fact sheets, so the population is children
   under 36 months. The question is asked only about
   each mother's most recent birth; children who were never breastfed (`m4 = 94`) count as 0.
2. **Fever/ARI treatment.** A&M's indicator is "children with **fever or symptoms of
   ARI** ... taken to a health facility or health provider". The population is children with fever, or with ARI symptoms (cough with short,
   rapid breaths and a chest problem), and the child counts as taken to a provider if **any** place
   in `h32a-h32x` was a health facility or provider. Pharmacy, shop, traditional healer,
   friend/relative and "other" are excluded; this reproduces FR339 Table 9.9 exactly. The letters
   differ by round: `h32k, u, v, w, x` in NFHS-4; `h32k, s, t, u, x` in NFHS-5.
3. **ORS and zinc:** "don't know" counts as not given, as in FR339 Table 9.11.

```{r s01-table2-outcomes}
## Places that do NOT count as a health facility or provider. FR339's footnote names pharmacy,
## shop and traditional healer; friend/relative and "other" are not facilities or providers either,
## and excluding them reproduces FR339 Table 9.9 exactly (73.2%).
NOT_PROVIDER <- list(nfhs4 = c("h32k", "h32u", "h32v", "h32w", "h32x"),   # pharmacy, shop, trad. healer, friend/relative, other
                     nfhs5 = c("h32k", "h32s", "h32t", "h32u", "h32x"))   # pharmacy, shop, trad. healer, friend/relative, other
provider_vars <- lapply(NOT_PROVIDER, function(x) setdiff(paste0("h32", letters[1:24]), x))

took_to_provider <- function(df, round) {
  vars <- intersect(provider_vars[[round]], names(df))
  as.integer(rowSums(sapply(df[vars], function(v) v %in% 1)) > 0)
}

nfhs_mega <- nfhs_mega %>%
  mutate(
    ## -- Child age in months, DHS standard, same formula in both rounds --
    age_months = v008 - b3,

    ## -- Underweight: weight-for-age z < -2 (hw71; 9996+ = flagged) --
    waz         = ifelse(hw71 >= 9996, NA, hw71) / 100,
    underweight = as.integer(waz < -2),

    ## -- MCP card: asked only for registered pregnancies (last birth), so NA otherwise --
    mcp_card = as.integer(mcp_card_raw == 1),

    ## -- Breastfed within 1 hour: children under 3, most recent birth --
    ##    m34: 0 = immediately, 100 = within first hour, 101+ = later, 199/299 = number missing
    breastfed_within_1hr = case_when(
      age_months >= 36                ~ NA_integer_,      # under-3 only
      m4 == 94                        ~ 0L,               # never breastfed
      m34 %in% c(0, 100)              ~ 1L,
      m34 %in% c(199, 299)            ~ NA_integer_,      # don't know
      !is.na(m34)                     ~ 0L,
      TRUE                            ~ NA_integer_
    ),

    ## -- ORS and zinc: among children with diarrhoea in the last two weeks (h11 = 1 or 2) --
    had_diarrhea = as.integer(h11 %in% c(1, 2)),
    ##    "Don't know" (8) counts as not given, as in FR339 Table 9.11
    ors_given  = if_else(had_diarrhea == 1, as.integer(h13 %in% c(1, 2)), NA_integer_),
    zinc_given = if_else(had_diarrhea == 1, as.integer(h15e %in% 1),      NA_integer_),

    ## -- Fever or ARI symptoms in the last two weeks --
    had_fever = as.integer(h22 == 1),
    had_ari   = as.integer(h31 %in% c(1, 2) & h31b == 1 & h31c %in% c(1, 3)),
    fever_or_ari = as.integer(had_fever == 1 | had_ari == 1)
  )

## Taken to a health facility or provider, computed separately per round because
## the h32 letters mean different places in NFHS-4 and NFHS-5.
nfhs_mega$to_provider <- NA_integer_
for (r in c("nfhs4", "nfhs5")) {
  idx <- nfhs_mega$survey_round == r
  nfhs_mega$to_provider[idx] <- took_to_provider(nfhs_mega[idx, ], r)
}
nfhs_mega <- nfhs_mega %>%
  mutate(
    fever_treatment_sought = if_else(fever_or_ari == 1, to_provider, NA_integer_),
    fever_only_treated     = if_else(had_fever == 1,    to_provider, NA_integer_)  # for the FR339 check only
  )

## Check 1: age. How often v008 - b3 disagrees with the alternative age variables (hw1, b19).
nfhs_mega %>%
  mutate(old_age = if_else(survey_round == "nfhs4", hw1, b19)) %>%
  group_by(survey_round) %>%
  summarise(children        = n(),
            old_age_missing = sum(is.na(old_age)),
            disagree        = sum(!is.na(old_age) & old_age != age_months),
            max_gap_months  = max(abs(old_age - age_months), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  print()

## Check 2: children in each outcome and weighted %, by round.
nfhs_mega %>%
  group_by(survey_round) %>%
  summarise(across(c(underweight, mcp_card, breastfed_within_1hr, ors_given, zinc_given,
                     fever_treatment_sought, fever_only_treated),
                   list(n = ~ sum(!is.na(.)),
                        pct = ~ round(weighted.mean(., weight, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1)))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-survey_round, names_to = c("indicator", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "^(.*)_(n|pct)$") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey_round, values_from = c(n, pct)) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

## 1.9 Diet outcomes: minimum dietary diversity, meal frequency, acceptable diet

A&M's two diet outcomes are "breastfeeding children age 6-23 months receiving an adequate diet"
and the same for non-breastfeeding children. Both are built here following the NFHS national
reports (FR339 and FR375, Table 10.10), and reproduce them (see the validation section).

**Population:** each mother's youngest child aged 6-23 months who lives with her. The feeding
questions are asked only about this child.

**Age.** NFHS-4: interview date minus birth date (`v008 - b3`); NFHS-5: `b19`. These are
the age variables each round's own report uses: with them, the weighted number of children matches
FR339 exactly (58,650 breastfed, 11,040 non-breastfed) and FR375 to within 5 (52,683; 9,570). Using
`hw1` instead would drop about 4,000 unmeasured NFHS-4 children.

**Food groups, the same in both rounds:**

| Group | Variables |
|---|---|
| Dairy | `v411` milk, `v411a` formula, `v414p` cheese/yogurt/milk products, `v414v` yogurt |
| Grains, roots, tubers | `v412a` fortified baby food, `v414e` grains, `v414f` tubers |
| Vitamin A fruits and vegetables | `v414i`, `v414j`, `v414k` |
| Other fruits and vegetables | `v414l` |
| Eggs | `v414g` |
| Meat, fish, poultry | `v414a` chicken/duck, `v414m` organ meat, `v414n` fish, `v414t` other meat |
| Legumes and nuts | `v414o` |

With these groups, NFHS-4 reproduces FR339 Table 10.10 exactly.

**Definition: each round follows its own national report.**

- Breastfed (`m4 = 95`), both rounds: 4+ of the 7 groups (equivalently, NFHS-5's 5+ of 8 with breast
  milk as a group), **and** solid/semi-solid feeds at least 2 times (age 6-8 months) or 3 times (9-23).
- Not breastfed: milk feeds at least 2 times, **and** 4+ of the 6 groups other than dairy, **and**
  solid feeds plus milk feeds at least 4 times. **NFHS-5 only** (FR375 Table 10.10, footnote 5):
  at least one of those feeds must be solid.
- Minimum dietary diversity (reported, not an A&M outcome): 4+ of 7 groups in NFHS-4 (FR339);
  5+ of 8 groups, breast milk counted, in NFHS-5 (FR375).

Consequence: the non-breastfed MAD definition is stricter in NFHS-5, so
part of any NFHS-4 to NFHS-5 change in that outcome reflects the definition. Breastfed MAD is
unaffected.

```{r s01-diet}
cnt <- function(x) ifelse(!is.na(x) & x <= 7, x, 0)   # feed counts; 8 = don't know counts as 0
yes <- function(...) as.integer(Reduce(`|`, lapply(list(...), function(v) v %in% 1)))

diet <- nfhs_mega %>%
  mutate(diet_age = if_else(survey_round == "nfhs4", age_months, as.numeric(b19))) %>%
  filter(b9 == 0, diet_age < 24) %>%                         # living with mother, under 2
  group_by(survey_round, v001, v002, v003) %>%
  slice_min(bidx, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%              # youngest child of each mother
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(diet_age >= 6) %>%
  mutate(
    breastfed = as.integer(m4 %in% 95),
    fg_dairy  = yes(v411, v411a, v414p, v414v),
    fg_grain  = yes(v412a, v414e, v414f),
    fg_vita   = yes(v414i, v414j, v414k),
    fg_ofv    = yes(v414l),
    fg_egg    = yes(v414g),
    fg_flesh  = yes(v414a, v414m, v414n, v414t),               #
    fg_legume = yes(v414o),
    n_groups         = fg_dairy + fg_grain + fg_vita + fg_ofv + fg_egg + fg_flesh + fg_legume,
    n_groups_nodairy = n_groups - fg_dairy,
    solid_feeds = cnt(m39),
    milk_feeds  = cnt(v469e) + cnt(v469f) + cnt(v469x),
    mdd = if_else(survey_round == "nfhs4",
                  as.integer(n_groups >= 4),                  # FR339: 4+ of 7
                  as.integer(n_groups + breastfed >= 5)),     # FR375: 5+ of 8, breast milk a group
    mmf = case_when(
      breastfed == 1 ~ as.integer((diet_age < 9 & solid_feeds >= 2) | (diet_age >= 9 & solid_feeds >= 3)),
      survey_round == "nfhs4" ~ as.integer(solid_feeds + milk_feeds >= 4),
      TRUE ~ as.integer(solid_feeds + milk_feeds >= 4 & solid_feeds >= 1)   # NFHS-5: 1+ solid feed
    ),
    mad = if_else(breastfed == 1,
                  as.integer(n_groups >= 4 & mmf == 1),
                  as.integer(milk_feeds >= 2 & n_groups_nodairy >= 4 & mmf == 1)),
    mad_breastfed    = if_else(breastfed == 1, mad, NA_integer_),
    mad_nonbreastfed = if_else(breastfed == 0, mad, NA_integer_)
  ) %>%
  select(survey_round, v001, v002, v003, bidx, diet_age, breastfed, n_groups,
         mdd, mmf, mad, mad_breastfed, mad_nonbreastfed)

## Attach to the child-level data; children outside the population get NA.
nfhs_mega <- nfhs_mega %>%
  select(-any_of(c("diet_age", "breastfed", "n_groups", "mdd", "mmf", "mad",
                   "mad_breastfed", "mad_nonbreastfed"))) %>%
  left_join(diet, by = c("survey_round", "v001", "v002", "v003", "bidx"))
stopifnot(nrow(nfhs_mega) == nrow(kr4) + nrow(kr5))

## Check: population size (weighted, compare with FR339/FR375 Table 10.10) and %s
diet %>%
  mutate(w = nfhs_mega$weight[match(paste(survey_round, v001, v002, v003, bidx),
                                    paste(nfhs_mega$survey_round, nfhs_mega$v001, nfhs_mega$v002,
                                          nfhs_mega$v003, nfhs_mega$bidx))]) %>%
  group_by(survey_round, breastfed) %>%
  summarise(children = n(), weighted_n = round(sum(w)),
            mdd = round(weighted.mean(mdd, w) * 100, 1),
            mmf = round(weighted.mean(mmf, w) * 100, 1),
            mad = round(weighted.mean(mad, w) * 100, 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  print()
```

## 1.10 Remaining Table 2 outcomes: IFA, home births, vaccination

Each definition was tested against the national reports (results in the validation section).

- **IFA 100+ days:** mother's most recent birth in the last five years (`midx = 1`); took iron/folic
  acid for 100 days or more (`m46` 100-997). Mothers not asked, because they took none, count as 0.
  Reproduces FR339 and FR375 Table 8.7 exactly (30.3, 44.1).
- **Home births by skilled personnel:** share of **all** births in the last five years that were at
  home (`m15` 10-13) **and** attended by a doctor, nurse/ANM/midwife/LHV or other health personnel
  (`m3a-m3c`). An unconditional share.
- **Full vaccination (either source):** living children 12-23 months with BCG, 3 doses of DPT or
  pentavalent, 3 doses of polio (excluding the birth dose) and measles, by card or mother's report.
- **Full vaccination (card only):** among children whose card was seen (`h1 = 1`), the same
  vaccines recorded on the card (codes 1 or 3). In NFHS-5, measles code 4 ("vaccination identified")
  also counts: without it the value is 66.2%, far from the published 83.8%; with it, 83.1%.

```{r s01-remaining-outcomes}
rec <- function(v, codes) v %in% codes
nfhs_mega <- nfhs_mega %>%
  mutate(
    ## -- IFA 100+ days: most recent birth only --
    ifa_100days = if_else(midx %in% 1, as.integer(ifa_days %in% 100:997), NA_integer_),   # ifa_days = m46, renamed in 1.4

    ## -- Home birth attended by skilled personnel, among all births --
    home_birth_skilled = as.integer(delivery_place %in% 10:13 &
                                    (m3a %in% 1 | m3b %in% 1 | m3c %in% 1)),

    ## -- Vaccination: living children 12-23 months; age as in the diet section --
    vacc_age  = if_else(survey_round == "nfhs4", age_months, as.numeric(b19)),
    vacc_pop  = b5 %in% 1 & vacc_age >= 12 & vacc_age <= 23,
    measles_codes_either = if_else(survey_round == "nfhs5", "1,2,3,4", "1,2,3"),
    vacc_either = if_else(vacc_pop, as.integer(
      rec(h2, 1:3) & (rec(h3, 1:3) | rec(h51, 1:3)) & (rec(h5, 1:3) | rec(h52, 1:3)) &
      (rec(h7, 1:3) | rec(h53, 1:3)) & rec(h4, 1:3) & rec(h6, 1:3) & rec(h8, 1:3) &
      (rec(h9, 1:3) | (survey_round == "nfhs5" & rec(h9, 4)))), NA_integer_),
    vacc_card_only = if_else(vacc_pop & h1 %in% 1, as.integer(
      rec(h2, c(1, 3)) & (rec(h3, c(1, 3)) | rec(h51, c(1, 3))) & (rec(h5, c(1, 3)) | rec(h52, c(1, 3))) &
      (rec(h7, c(1, 3)) | rec(h53, c(1, 3))) & rec(h4, c(1, 3)) & rec(h6, c(1, 3)) & rec(h8, c(1, 3)) &
      (rec(h9, c(1, 3)) | (survey_round == "nfhs5" & rec(h9, 4)))), NA_integer_)
  ) %>%
  select(-measles_codes_either)

## Check: population sizes and weighted %, by round
nfhs_mega %>%
  group_by(survey_round) %>%
  summarise(across(c(ifa_100days, home_birth_skilled, vacc_either, vacc_card_only),
                   list(n = ~ sum(!is.na(.)),
                        pct = ~ round(weighted.mean(., weight, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1)))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-survey_round, names_to = c("indicator", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "^(.*)_(n|pct)$") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey_round, values_from = c(n, pct)) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

## 1.11 Sex ratio at birth

Girls per 1,000 boys among births in the five years before the interview (`v008 - b3` of 0-59
months), from the births (BR) file, weighted. Computed directly at district level, because it is a
ratio of counts rather than a per-child indicator.

Two things to know. First, national values come out at 914 (NFHS-4) and 925 (NFHS-5), against 919
and 929 in the national fact sheets; the source of the 4-5 point gap has not been identified.
Second, a district has about 400 births per round, so district sex ratios are noisy: a
single district's value can move by 50 or more by chance alone.

```{r s01-srb}
BR_VARS <- c("v005", "v008", "b3", "b4")
read_br <- function(path, distvar, round_label) {
  read_dta(path, col_select = all_of(c(BR_VARS, distvar))) %>%
    zap_labels() %>%
    filter(v008 - b3 >= 0, v008 - b3 <= 59) %>%              # born in the last five years
    transmute(distcode = as.numeric(.data[[distvar]]), survey_round = round_label,
              weight = v005 / 1e6, female = as.integer(b4 == 2))
}
br <- bind_rows(
  checkpoint("br4", BR_VARS, read_br(dhs_file("IABR74FL.DTA"), "sdistri", "nfhs4")),
  checkpoint("br5", BR_VARS, read_br(dhs_file("IABR7EFL.DTA"), "sdist",   "nfhs5"))
)

srb_national <- br %>% group_by(survey_round) %>%
  summarise(births = n(),
            srb = round(1000 * sum(weight * female) / sum(weight * (1 - female))))
print(srb_national)

district_srb <- br %>% group_by(distcode, survey_round) %>%
  summarise(srb = 1000 * sum(weight * female) / sum(weight * (1 - female)),
            n_births = n(), .groups = "drop")
summary(district_srb$n_births)
```

## 1.12 Collapse to district level and save

Every child-level indicator becomes a weighted percentage per district and round (weight = `v005`,
checked earlier to give the same district values as the state weights). Toilet and water come from
the household-level build (1.7) and sex ratio from 1.11. Column names match what the later stages
read. For each indicator the panel also stores `n_<indicator>`, the number of children behind the
district value, so thin cells are visible.

Three files are saved in `data/intermediate/`:

| File | Contents | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `district_outcomes_panel.csv` | one row per district and round; all Table 2 outcomes, the NFHS covariates, counts | Stage 05 (crosswalk), Stages 08-10 |
| `district_covariates_baseline.csv` | NFHS-4 only; the 9 NFHS-built propensity-score covariates | Stages 03, 05, 06 |
| `nfhs_mega.rds` | child-level data, both rounds | Stage 02 (district names) and checks |

```{r s01-collapse}
## Child-level indicators and the column names later stages expect.
## Two are renamed for later stages: breastfed_within_1hr, fever_treatment_sought.
CHILD_VARS <- c("stunted", "wasted", "severely_wasted", "underweight",
                "anc_first_trimester", "anc_4plus_visits", "full_anc", "institutional_birth",
                "mcp_card", "breastfed_1hr", "ors_given", "zinc_given", "fever_treated",
                "mdd", "mmf", "mad", "mad_breastfed", "mad_nonbreastfed",
                "ifa_100days", "home_birth_skilled", "vacc_either", "vacc_card_only")

wpct <- function(x, w) if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else weighted.mean(x, w, na.rm = TRUE) * 100

child_panel <- nfhs_mega %>%
  mutate(breastfed_1hr = breastfed_within_1hr, fever_treated = fever_treatment_sought) %>%
  group_by(distcode, survey_round) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(CHILD_VARS),
                   list(pct = ~ wpct(.x, weight),
                        n   = ~ sum(!is.na(.x)),
                        w   = ~ sum(weight[!is.na(.x)])),   # used only for the check below
                   .names = "{.fn}_{.col}"),
            n_children = n(), .groups = "drop")

district_outcomes_panel <- child_panel %>%
  left_join(district_hh_covariates, by = c("distcode", "survey_round")) %>%
  left_join(district_srb,           by = c("distcode", "survey_round"))

## Check 1: one row per district and round, 640 + 707, nothing lost in the joins.
stopifnot(nrow(district_outcomes_panel) == 640 + 707,
          !any(duplicated(district_outcomes_panel[, c("distcode", "survey_round")])),
          all(!is.na(district_outcomes_panel$pct_no_individual_toilet)),
          all(!is.na(district_outcomes_panel$srb)))
print(table(district_outcomes_panel$survey_round))

## Check 2: averaging the district values back up (weighted by each district's total weight)
## must give exactly the national figure. A difference means the collapse lost or doubled children.
national_from_children <- nfhs_mega %>%
  mutate(breastfed_1hr = breastfed_within_1hr, fever_treated = fever_treatment_sought) %>%
  group_by(survey_round) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(CHILD_VARS), ~ wpct(.x, weight)))
national_from_districts <- sapply(CHILD_VARS, function(v) {
  sapply(national_from_children$survey_round, function(r) {
    d <- district_outcomes_panel[district_outcomes_panel$survey_round == r, ]
    weighted.mean(d[[paste0("pct_", v)]], d[[paste0("w_", v)]], na.rm = TRUE)
  })
})
max_gap <- max(abs(as.matrix(national_from_children[, CHILD_VARS]) - national_from_districts))
cat("Largest gap between national-from-children and national-from-districts:", max_gap, "\n")
stopifnot(max_gap < 1e-8)

## Check 3: how many district values rest on fewer than 25 children (NFHS suppresses these).
district_outcomes_panel %>%
  select(survey_round, starts_with("n_"), -n_children, -n_households) %>%
  group_by(survey_round) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(.x < 25, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-survey_round, names_to = "indicator", values_to = "districts_below_25") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey_round, values_from = districts_below_25) %>%
  filter(nfhs4 > 0 | nfhs5 > 0) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

## Save. The w_ columns were only for Check 2.
district_outcomes_panel <- district_outcomes_panel %>% select(-starts_with("w_"))

BASELINE_COVARIATES <- c("pct_stunted", "pct_wasted", "pct_severely_wasted",
                         "pct_anc_first_trimester", "pct_anc_4plus_visits", "pct_full_anc",
                         "pct_institutional_birth", "pct_no_individual_toilet", "pct_no_water_access")
district_covariates_baseline <- district_outcomes_panel %>%
  filter(survey_round == "nfhs4") %>%
  select(distcode, all_of(BASELINE_COVARIATES), n_children, n_households)

write_csv(district_outcomes_panel,      file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_outcomes_panel.csv"))
write_csv(district_covariates_baseline, file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_covariates_baseline.csv"))
saveRDS(nfhs_mega,                      file.path(INTER_DIR, "nfhs_mega.rds"))
cat("Saved:", nrow(district_outcomes_panel), "district-round rows;",
    nrow(district_covariates_baseline), "NFHS-4 districts;", nrow(nfhs_mega), "children\n")
```

## 1.13 Validation record for Stage 01

Every check run on Stage 01 so far, in one place. The chunk recomputes each value from the data
in memory and compares it with the benchmark, so rerunning it after any change shows immediately
whether something has moved. Two kinds of check:

- **Internal:** the data behave as they must (no duplicated households, joins keep every child,
  district codes agree across files).
- **External:** constructed indicators against the officially published NFHS figures. Sources:
  FR339 = NFHS-4 India national report; FR375 = NFHS-5 India national report; FS6 = NFHS-6 India Fact Sheet (NFHS-5 column);
  OF43 Compendium = DHS Program, NFHS-5 India and State Factsheet Compendium Phase II (NFHS-5 and
  NFHS-4 columns), dhsprogram.com/pubs/pdf/OF43.   Every benchmark is read from one of these documents; none is recalled.

Tolerance: 0.2 points where our definition is the published one. ANC indicators get 1.0 point,
because the official figures count each mother's most recent birth while ours count children.
NFHS-5 diet (MAD) gets 0.5: age from b19 and food groups differ slightly from FR375 (section 1.9).
NFHS-5 toilet and water are not compared, because NFHS-4 definitions are used in both rounds.

```{r s01-validation}
wpct <- function(x, w) round(weighted.mean(x, w, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1)
n4 <- nfhs_mega %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs4")
n5 <- nfhs_mega %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs5")
h4 <- hh %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs4")

## Internal checks: TRUE = passed
internal <- tibble::tribble(
  ~check,                                                        ~passed,
  "NFHS-4 HR: one row per household",                            !any(duplicated(hr4[, c("v001", "v002")])),
  "NFHS-5 HR: one row per household",                            !any(duplicated(hr5[, c("v001", "v002")])),
  "HR join keeps every child (both rounds)",                     nrow(nfhs_mega) == nrow(kr4) + nrow(kr5),
  "Every child has a household record",                          all(!is.na(nfhs_mega$hv009)),
  "KR and HR district codes identical (NFHS-4)",                 setequal(unique(kr4$distcode), unique(hr4$hh_distcode)),
  "KR and HR district codes identical (NFHS-5)",                 setequal(unique(kr5$distcode), unique(hr5$hh_distcode)),
  ## b19 (age) and h51-h53 (pentavalent doses) do not exist in NFHS-4: pentavalent replaced DPT later.
  "Only b19, h51-h53 missing from KR (NFHS-4); nothing from NFHS-5", setequal(kr4_missing, c("b19", "h51", "h52", "h53")) &&
                                                                  length(kr5_missing) == 0
)

## External checks against published figures
external <- tibble::tribble(
  ~indicator,                   ~round,  ~ours,                                          ~published, ~source,                         ~tol,
  "Districts",                  "NFHS-4", n_distinct(kr4$distcode),                       640,       "FR339 Appendix C (sample design)", 0,
  "Households interviewed",     "NFHS-4", nrow(hr4),                                      601509,    "FR339 Table 1.1",               0,
  "Stunted",                    "NFHS-4", wpct(n4$stunted, n4$weight),                    38.4,      "FR339 Table 10.1",              0.2,
  "Wasted",                     "NFHS-4", wpct(n4$wasted, n4$weight),                     21.0,      "FR339 Table 10.1",              0.2,
  "Severely wasted",            "NFHS-4", wpct(n4$severely_wasted, n4$weight),            7.4,       "FR339 Table 10.1",              0.2,
  "4+ ANC visits",              "NFHS-4", wpct(n4$anc_4plus_visits, n4$weight),           51.2,      "FR339 Table 8.5",               1.0,
  "ANC in first trimester",     "NFHS-4", wpct(n4$anc_first_trimester, n4$weight),        58.6,      "FR339 Table 8.5",               1.0,
  "Full ANC",                   "NFHS-4", wpct(n4$full_anc, n4$weight),                   20.9,      "FR339 Table 8.26",              1.0,
  "Institutional births",       "NFHS-4", wpct(n4$institutional_birth, n4$weight),        78.9,      "FR339 Table 8.13",              0.2,
  "Improved sanitation (hh)",   "NFHS-4", wpct(h4$toilet_improved, h4$hh_weight),         48.4,      "FR339 Table 2.2",               0.2,
  "Improved sanitation (pop)",  "NFHS-4", wpct(h4$toilet_improved, h4$pop_weight),        48.4,      "FR339 Table 2.2",               0.2,
  "Improved water (hh)",        "NFHS-4", wpct(h4$water_improved, h4$hh_weight),          89.9,      "FR339 Table 2.1",               0.2,
  "Improved water (pop)",       "NFHS-4", wpct(h4$water_improved, h4$pop_weight),         90.2,      "FR339 Table 2.1",               0.2,
```

# Stage 02: Aspirational District (treatment) flags

Attaches the treatment indicator to every district and round:

- **Source of the flags:** the official list of 112 Aspirational Districts (NITI Aayog), with 2018
  names from NITI's March 2018 Baseline Ranking and a cross-check against UNDP's Appraisal
  (`data/lookups/adp_official_list.csv` and its README).
- **Matching to NFHS codes:** automatic on the current or 2018 name within the state; the 23 other
  cases come from `data/lookups/adp_manual_matches.csv`, each with a written reason.
- **Districts created after 2011:** in NFHS-4, Kondagaon and Sukma sit inside Bastar and Dantewada,
  which are themselves ADs, so those parents are fully treated. Namsai, Komaram Bheem Asifabad,
  Jayashankar Bhupalpally and Bhadradri Kothagudem sit inside parents that also contain non-AD area
  (Lohit, Adilabad, Warangal, Khammam). These are flagged `adp_mixed_parent = 1` and dropped with the
  other split parents in the NOSPLIT sample (Stage 05).

## 2.1 District and state names from the NFHS files

```{r s02-names}
## Value labels only (n_max = 1), so this is quick. Names are never typed by hand.
labels_of <- function(path, var) {
  x <- read_dta(dhs_file(path), col_select = all_of(var), n_max = 1)
  l <- attr(x[[var]], "labels")
  tibble(code = as.numeric(l), label = names(l))
}
names_for_round <- function(path, distvar, round_label) {
  nfhs_mega %>%
    filter(survey_round == round_label) %>%
    distinct(distcode, v024) %>%
    left_join(labels_of(path, distvar) %>% rename(distcode = code, district_name = label), by = "distcode") %>%
    left_join(labels_of(path, "v024") %>% rename(v024 = code, state_name = label), by = "v024") %>%
    transmute(distcode, survey_round = round_label, district_name, state_name)
}
district_names <- bind_rows(names_for_round("IAKR74FL.DTA", "sdistri", "nfhs4"),
                            names_for_round("IAKR7EFL.DTA", "sdist",   "nfhs5"))

## Check: one name per district and round, none missing, 640 + 707.
stopifnot(nrow(district_names) == 640 + 707,
          !any(duplicated(district_names[, c("distcode", "survey_round")])),
          all(!is.na(district_names$district_name)), all(!is.na(district_names$state_name)))
```

## 2.2 Match the official list to NFHS district codes

```{r s02-crosswalk}
norm <- function(x) gsub("[^a-z]", "", tolower(gsub("&", "and", x)))

official <- read_csv(file.path(LOOKUP_DIR, "adp_official_list.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
manual   <- read_csv(file.path(LOOKUP_DIR, "adp_manual_matches.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

## Automatic matches: same state, and NFHS name equal to the current or the 2018 name.
auto <- tidyr::crossing(official %>% select(state, district = district_current_list,
                                            district_2018 = district_2018_ranking),
                        survey_round = c("nfhs4", "nfhs5")) %>%
  anti_join(manual, by = c("state", "district", "survey_round")) %>%
  inner_join(district_names, by = "survey_round", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  filter(norm(state) == norm(state_name),
         norm(district_name) == norm(district) |
           (!is.na(district_2018) & norm(district_name) == norm(district_2018))) %>%
  mutate(match_type = if_else(norm(district_name) == norm(district), "exact", "2018 name"),
         note = if_else(match_type == "2018 name", paste0("matched on 2018 name '", district_2018, "'"), NA_character_)) %>%
  select(state, district, survey_round, distcode, match_type, note)

adp_crosswalk <- bind_rows(auto, manual %>% mutate(distcode = as.numeric(distcode))) %>%
  left_join(district_names %>% select(distcode, survey_round, nfhs_name = district_name),
            by = c("distcode", "survey_round")) %>%
  arrange(survey_round, state, district)

## Check: every one of the 112 ADs matched exactly once in each round, to a code that exists.
per_ad <- count(adp_crosswalk, state, district, survey_round)
stopifnot(nrow(per_ad) == 2 * 112, all(per_ad$n == 1), all(!is.na(adp_crosswalk$nfhs_name)))
print(count(adp_crosswalk, survey_round, match_type) %>%
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey_round, values_from = n))
write_csv(adp_crosswalk, file.path(INTER_DIR, "adp_nfhs_crosswalk.csv"))
```

## 2.3 Attach the flags

```{r s02-flags}
## NFHS-4 parents that contain an AD created after 2011 AND non-AD area. A parent that is itself
## matched as an AD (Bastar, Dantewada) is fully treated and not mixed.
created_parents <- adp_crosswalk %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs4", match_type == "created after 2011")
own_ads         <- adp_crosswalk %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs4", match_type != "created after 2011")
mixed_parents   <- setdiff(created_parents$distcode, own_ads$distcode)

treated <- adp_crosswalk %>% distinct(distcode, survey_round) %>% mutate(adp_flag = 1L)

district_panel_adp <- district_outcomes_panel %>%
  left_join(district_names, by = c("distcode", "survey_round")) %>%
  left_join(treated,        by = c("distcode", "survey_round")) %>%
  mutate(adp_flag = coalesce(adp_flag, 0L),
         adp_mixed_parent = as.integer(survey_round == "nfhs4" & distcode %in% mixed_parents)) %>%
  relocate(distcode, survey_round, district_name, state_name, adp_flag, adp_mixed_parent)

## Check 1: treated districts per round (NFHS-4: 110 codes for 112 ADs, because Bastar and
## Dantewada each contain two ADs; NFHS-5: 112). Mixed parents: Lohit, Adilabad, Warangal, Khammam.
print(count(district_panel_adp, survey_round, adp_flag))
print(district_panel_adp %>% filter(adp_mixed_parent == 1) %>% select(distcode, district_name, state_name))
stopifnot(sum(district_panel_adp$adp_flag[district_panel_adp$survey_round == "nfhs4"]) == 110,
          sum(district_panel_adp$adp_flag[district_panel_adp$survey_round == "nfhs5"]) == 112,
          length(mixed_parents) == 4)

## Save: new files, so the Stage 01 outputs are never overwritten.
district_baseline_adp <- district_panel_adp %>%
  filter(survey_round == "nfhs4") %>%
  select(distcode, district_name, state_name, adp_flag, adp_mixed_parent,
         all_of(BASELINE_COVARIATES), n_children, n_households)
write_csv(district_panel_adp,    file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_panel_adp.csv"))
write_csv(district_baseline_adp, file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_baseline_adp.csv"))
```


# Stage 03: External propensity-score covariates

Three of Agarwal & Mishra's Table 1 covariates come from outside NFHS. Each source is matched to NFHS-4
districts (2011 boundaries) through `data/lookups/external_district_matches.csv`, which lists every
source row, its NFHS-4 district and how it was matched (see the README in `data/lookups/`).

- **Landless households dependent on manual labour (SECC 2011):** the "All" row per district (the
  category rows overlap, so summing them would count households more than once).
- **Unelectrified households (Saubhagya, as on 10 Oct 2017):** for districts split after 2011, the
  household counts are summed and the share recomputed. Districts absent from Saubhagya are set
  to 0: they had no unelectrified households.
- **Adverse pupil-teacher ratio (U-DISE 2015-16):** schools with PTR above 30 (primary) or 35 (upper
  primary), pooled over all schools offering each level; counts summed for split districts.
- **Not available:** elementary dropout rate and the two PMGSY-III road variables, so the
  propensity score uses 12 of A&M's 15 covariates.

## 3.1 Build the three covariates

```{r s03-external}
matches <- read_csv(file.path(LOOKUP_DIR, "external_district_matches.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
match_for <- function(src) matches %>% filter(source == src) %>% select(source_state, source_district, distcode)

## -- SECC 2011: "All" row only
secc <- read_csv(file.path(EXT_RAW_DIR, "socio-economic-caste-census-2011.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(category == "All") %>%
  select(source_state = state_name, source_district = district_name, tot_hh, landless_hh_manual_labor) %>%
  left_join(match_for("secc"), by = c("source_state", "source_district"))
stopifnot(nrow(secc) == 631, all(!is.na(secc$distcode)))          # every SECC district matched
secc_d <- secc %>% group_by(distcode) %>%
  summarise(pct_landless_manual_labor = 100 * sum(landless_hh_manual_labor) / sum(tot_hh), .groups = "drop")

## -- U-DISE 2015-16: counts summed, then the pooled share
udise <- read_csv(file.path(EXT_RAW_DIR, "2015_16_Districtwise.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(source_state = STATNAME, source_district = DISTNAME,
            schools_primary = SCH1 + SCH2 + SCH3 + SCH6,           # all school types with a primary level
            schools_upper   = SCH2 + SCH3 + SCH4 + SCH6,           # all school types with an upper-primary level
            adverse = PPTR30 + UPTR35) %>%                         # primary PTR > 30, upper-primary PTR > 35
  left_join(match_for("udise"), by = c("source_state", "source_district"))
stopifnot(nrow(udise) == 680, all(!is.na(udise$distcode)))
udise_d <- udise %>% group_by(distcode) %>%
  summarise(pct_adverse_ptr = 100 * sum(adverse) / sum(schools_primary + schools_upper), .groups = "drop")

## -- Saubhagya, balance as on 10 Oct 2017: household counts summed, then the share
elec <- read_csv(file.path(EXT_RAW_DIR, "unelectrified_household_covariate.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(source_state = state, source_district = district, total_households, balance_unelectrified_hh) %>%
  left_join(match_for("unelectrified"), by = c("source_state", "source_district"))
stopifnot(nrow(elec) == 637, all(!is.na(elec$distcode)))
elec_d <- elec %>% group_by(distcode) %>%
  summarise(pct_unelectrified = 100 * sum(balance_unelectrified_hh) / sum(total_households), .groups = "drop")

## -- Attach to the NFHS-4 baseline (Stage 02). Absent from Saubhagya = 0 (see above).
district_baseline_full <- district_baseline_adp %>%
  left_join(secc_d,  by = "distcode") %>%
  left_join(udise_d, by = "distcode") %>%
  left_join(elec_d,  by = "distcode") %>%
  mutate(pct_unelectrified = coalesce(pct_unelectrified, 0))
stopifnot(nrow(district_baseline_full) == 640)

## Check 1: which districts have no value (expected: SECC 9 fully urban districts; U-DISE 3).
district_baseline_full %>%
  filter(is.na(pct_landless_manual_labor) | is.na(pct_adverse_ptr)) %>%
  select(distcode, district_name, state_name, adp_flag, pct_landless_manual_labor, pct_adverse_ptr) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
cat("Districts set to 0 unelectrified (absent from Saubhagya):",
    sum(!district_baseline_full$distcode %in% elec_d$distcode), "\n")
```

## 3.2 Check against Agarwal & Mishra's Table 3

AD and non-AD means of the 12 covariates compared with A&M's Table 3 (their sample is 104 ADs and
495 non-ADs, so means are not expected to agree exactly).

```{r s03-checks}
## AD vs non-AD means (NFHS-4 districts, mixed parents excluded) against A&M Table 3
am_table3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~covariate,                    ~am_ad,  ~am_non_ad,
  "pct_landless_manual_labor",   30.2397, 24.5434,
  "pct_anc_first_trimester",     52.5760, 60.9505,
  "pct_anc_4plus_visits",        39.9740, 52.6638,
  "pct_full_anc",                14.6356, 21.6954,
  "pct_institutional_birth",     68.8885, 80.3258,
  "pct_stunted",                 42.8942, 34.8777,
  "pct_wasted",                  23.8192, 20.1223,
  "pct_severely_wasted",          8.9558,  7.4608,
  "pct_adverse_ptr",             28.9527, 22.8524,
  "pct_unelectrified",           23.1067, 12.8397,
  "pct_no_individual_toilet",    67.9798, 49.2710,
  "pct_no_water_access",         15.3510, 10.9193)
ours <- district_baseline_full %>%
  filter(adp_mixed_parent == 0) %>%
  group_by(adp_flag) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(am_table3$covariate), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), n = n()) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(adp_flag, n), names_to = "covariate") %>%
  mutate(group = if_else(adp_flag == 1, "ours_ad", "ours_non_ad")) %>%
  select(covariate, group, value) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = value)
print(left_join(am_table3, ours, by = "covariate") %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1))), n = Inf)
cat("Districts: ADs", sum(district_baseline_full$adp_flag == 1 & district_baseline_full$adp_mixed_parent == 0),
    "| non-ADs", sum(district_baseline_full$adp_flag == 0), "\n")

write_csv(district_baseline_full, file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_baseline_full.csv"))
```


# Stage 05: Linking the two rounds and the NOSPLIT sample

The difference-in-differences compares each district with itself in NFHS-4 and NFHS-5, so every
district in the sample must cover the same area in both rounds. Two facts make this more than a
join on district code:

- **Codes are not stable across rounds.** 61 districts keep their name but get a new code in
  NFHS-5; 9 of them are in the final sample (6 Delhi districts, Hyderabad, and Sangrur and Shahid
  Bhagat Singh Nagar, which swap codes 39 and 53). The rounds are therefore linked only through
  `data/lookups/nfhs4_nfhs5_district_links.csv`, never by raw code.
- **70 NFHS-5 districts were carved out of NFHS-4 districts.** What matters is the two survey
  frames, not legal dates: districts created before NFHS-5 but not sampled separately by it
  (Alipurduar, Kalimpong, Jhargram and others) leave their parent's area unchanged between rounds.

The links file has one row per NFHS-5 district: the NFHS-4 district it continues (`same`, `rename`)
or was carved from (`split_child`, with a second parent where the new district took land from two).
It was built once by `R/build_district_links.py`; each parent's source is recorded in the file
and in `data/lookups/district_split_sources.md` (LGD sub-district codes for 64 splits, NIC district
websites for Tripura, an unofficial list for Delhi's two splits).

**Sample rules:**

- **Same boundaries in both rounds (NOSPLIT):** drop every NFHS-4 district that lost land to a new district, as first or
  second parent, together with the new districts carved from it. Bastar and Dantewada are dropped
  with the rest.
- **Tripura:** Dhalai (AD) is kept; no official source names it as a parent.
- **Delhi:** the 6 unsplit districts are kept as non-AD controls.
- **Expected:** 582 districts in both rounds, 102 ADs and 480 non-ADs.

Treatment `adp_flag` is the NFHS-4 (baseline) flag. For every kept district it must equal the NFHS-5
flag, since the area is the same.

## 5.1 Read and check the links

```{r s05-links}
links <- read_csv(file.path(LOOKUP_DIR, "nfhs4_nfhs5_district_links.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
names4 <- district_panel_adp %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs4") %>% select(distcode, district_name)
names5 <- district_panel_adp %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs5") %>% select(distcode, district_name)

## Check 1: one row per NFHS-5 district; every NFHS-4 district is linked; names in the file are
## the names behind each code in this run (guards against a code meaning something else).
stopifnot(nrow(links) == 707, !any(duplicated(links$nfhs5_distcode)),
          setequal(links$nfhs5_distcode, names5$distcode),
          all(names4$distcode %in% links$nfhs4_distcode),
          all(links$nfhs5_district == names5$district_name[match(links$nfhs5_distcode, names5$distcode)]),
          all(links$nfhs4_district == names4$district_name[match(links$nfhs4_distcode, names4$distcode)]))
print(count(links, link_type))
print(count(links %>% filter(link_type == "split_child"), link_source))
```

## 5.2 Split parents, mixed parents and the NOSPLIT sample

```{r s05-nosplit}
## NFHS-4 districts that lost land: first or second parent of any NFHS-5 split child.
split_parents <- union(links$nfhs4_distcode[links$link_type == "split_child"],
                       na.omit(links$nfhs4_second_parent_distcode))

## Mixed parents, recomputed from the links: NFHS-4 districts whose NFHS-5 pieces have different
## AD status. Replaces the Stage 02 flag, which missed Dhubri, Firozpur and Karimnagar.
pieces <- bind_rows(links %>% select(nfhs4_distcode, nfhs5_distcode),
                    links %>% filter(!is.na(nfhs4_second_parent_distcode)) %>%
                      select(nfhs4_distcode = nfhs4_second_parent_distcode, nfhs5_distcode)) %>%
  left_join(district_panel_adp %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs5") %>%
              select(nfhs5_distcode = distcode, adp5 = adp_flag), by = "nfhs5_distcode")
mixed <- pieces %>% group_by(nfhs4_distcode) %>%
  summarise(mixed = min(adp5) != max(adp5), .groups = "drop") %>% filter(mixed)
print(names4 %>% filter(distcode %in% mixed$nfhs4_distcode))
stopifnot(all(mixed$nfhs4_distcode %in% split_parents))   # NOSPLIT drops every mixed parent

## One continuation per NFHS-4 district (same or rename).
continuation <- links %>% filter(link_type != "split_child") %>%
  select(distcode = nfhs4_distcode, nfhs5_distcode)
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(continuation$distcode)))

nosplit_map <- district_baseline_full %>%
  select(distcode, district_name, state_name, adp_flag) %>%
  mutate(split_parent = distcode %in% split_parents,
         mixed_parent = distcode %in% mixed$nfhs4_distcode) %>%
  left_join(continuation, by = "distcode") %>%
  left_join(district_panel_adp %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs5") %>%
              select(nfhs5_distcode = distcode, adp_flag_nfhs5 = adp_flag), by = "nfhs5_distcode")
sample_ids <- nosplit_map %>% filter(!split_parent)

## Check 2: sample size and composition.
cat("Dropped split parents:", sum(nosplit_map$split_parent),
    "| of which ADs:", sum(nosplit_map$split_parent & nosplit_map$adp_flag == 1), "\n")
print(nosplit_map %>% filter(split_parent, adp_flag == 1) %>% select(district_name, state_name, mixed_parent))
print(count(sample_ids, adp_flag))
stopifnot(nrow(sample_ids) == 582, sum(sample_ids$adp_flag) == 102,
          !anyNA(sample_ids$nfhs5_distcode), !any(duplicated(sample_ids$nfhs5_distcode)))

## Check 3: treatment is the same in both rounds for every kept district.
stopifnot(all(sample_ids$adp_flag == sample_ids$adp_flag_nfhs5))

## Check 4: code changes are handled. Sangrur must link to Sangrur, not to SBS Nagar.
cat("Kept districts whose code differs between rounds:",
    sum(sample_ids$distcode != sample_ids$nfhs5_distcode), "\n")
print(sample_ids %>% filter(district_name %in% c("sangrur", "shahid bhagat singh nagar")) %>%
        select(district_name, nfhs4_code = distcode, nfhs5_code = nfhs5_distcode))
```
