# Stage 06: Women's empowerment outcomes

This stage builds the empowerment outcomes for the 582 NOSPLIT districts, for two populations:
currently married women aged 15-49 and women aged 15-24.

| Outcome | Items | Population(s) |
|---|---|---|
| Household decision-making index | own health care, large purchases, visits to family, husband's earnings (`v743a/b/d/f`); 1 = respondent decides alone or jointly | married women 15-49; married women 15-24 |
| Healthcare access barrier index | permission, money, distance, not wanting to go alone (`v467b/c/d/f`); 1 = big problem | married women 15-49; all women 15-24 |
| Years of education | `v133`, single years | all women 15-24 |
| Water collection time | `v115`, minutes for one round trip, capped at 120 | married women 15-49; all women 15-24 |

Every outcome is computed for both populations, so later stages pick the ones they need.

**How the data were collected (checked against FR339 and FR375):**

- The decision-making questions are in the **state module**: every second household in a random 30%
  of clusters, about 15% of households, in both rounds. They were asked only of currently married
  women. The national reports state the module was designed for **state-level** estimates, so
  district means of the decision-making index are noisy.
- The barrier questions were asked of **all women**, so the barrier index is district-representative.
- `v115` comes from the household questionnaire (Q27): "How long does it take to go there, get
  water, and come back in one trip?" It is a **round trip**.
- Weights: the women's weight `v005`. Within each state it differs from the state weight only by a
  constant, so district means are the same with either. There is no separate state-module weight.

**Construction:**

1. **Indices** are the first principal component of the four items. The main index takes its
   weights from NFHS-4 only (6.4b), so that the weights cannot reflect the programme; a PCA on both
   rounds pooled (6.4) is kept for comparison. Both are unweighted and in SD units. The sign is
   fixed so that higher = more say (decision-making) and more barriers (barrier index).
2. **Districts** come from the Stage 05 sample (`district_nosplit_map.csv`), never raw codes.
3. **Water time** is capped at 120 minutes. The uncapped version is kept for the appendix (6.6).
4. **Water access (binary):** round trip of 30 minutes or less, counting water on the premises,
   labelled "collection time within 30 minutes (JMP time criterion)". The full JMP "basic service"
   (also an improved source) is built for the appendix.

```{r s06-settings}
WATER_CAP <- 120   # minutes; caps of 90 and 150 are checked in Stage 09

## Improved drinking-water sources, one definition for both rounds: FR375 Section 2.1
## ("piped water, public taps, standpipes, tube wells, boreholes, protected dug wells and springs,
## rainwater, tanker truck, cart with small tank, bottled water, and community reverse osmosis (RO)
## plants"). The codes differ by round (v113 value labels), so they are listed per round.
## FR339 counted bottled water and tanker/cart as unimproved; that older definition is only used
## below to validate the codes against FR339's published figure.
IMPROVED_WATER <- list(
  nfhs4 = c(11, 12, 13, 21, 31, 41, 51, 61, 62, 71, 72),       # 13 = public tap, 72 = community RO plant
  nfhs5 = c(11, 12, 13, 14, 21, 31, 41, 51, 61, 62, 71, 92))   # 13 = piped to neighbour, 14 = public tap, 92 = community RO plant
IMPROVED_WATER_FR339 <- c(11, 12, 13, 21, 31, 41, 51, 72)
```

## 6.1 Read the women's files

```{r s06-read}
## Every variable read from the women's (IR) file. Same variable and meaning in both rounds.
IR_VARS <- c(
  "v001", "v002", "v003",   # cluster, household, woman's line number
  "v005",                   # women's sample weight, 6 decimals
  "v012",                   # age in years
  "v024",                   # state
  "v502",                   # 1 = currently in union (married or living with a man)
  "ssmod",                  # 1 = household selected for the state module
  "v743a",                  # who decides on her own health care
  "v743b",                  # who decides on large household purchases
  "v743d",                  # who decides on visits to her family or relatives
  "v743f",                  # who decides what to do with the money her husband earns (7 = he has no earnings)
  "v467b",                  # getting medical help: getting permission to go (0 no, 1 big, 2 not big problem)
  "v467c",                  # getting medical help: getting money for treatment
  "v467d",                  # getting medical help: distance to the health facility
  "v467f",                  # getting medical help: not wanting to go alone
  "v115",                   # round-trip time to water source (0 delivered [NFHS-4], 996 on premises, 997 not de jure, 998 don't know)
  "v113",                   # source of drinking water (codes differ by round; see s06-settings)
  "v133")                   # education in single years (97 = inconsistent)

read_ir <- function(file, distvar, round_label) {
  read_dta(dhs_file(file), col_select = any_of(c(IR_VARS, distvar))) %>%
    zap_labels() %>%
    mutate(distcode = as.numeric(.data[[distvar]]), survey_round = round_label) %>%
    select(-all_of(distvar))
}
ir4e <- checkpoint("ir4_empowerment", IR_VARS, read_ir("IAIR74FL.DTA", "sdistri", "nfhs4"))
ir5e <- checkpoint("ir5_empowerment", IR_VARS, read_ir("IAIR7EFL.DTA", "sdist",   "nfhs5"))

## Check: every variable present, and all interviewed women read (FR339: 699,686; FR375: 724,115).
stopifnot(all(IR_VARS %in% names(ir4e)), all(IR_VARS %in% names(ir5e)),
          nrow(ir4e) == 699686, nrow(ir5e) == 724115)
```

## 6.2 Code the items

```{r s06-items}
has_say     <- function(x) case_when(x %in% 1:3 ~ 1, x %in% 4:6 ~ 0, TRUE ~ NA_real_)   # 7 "no earnings" -> NA
big_problem <- function(x) case_when(x == 1 ~ 1, x %in% c(0, 2) ~ 0, TRUE ~ NA_real_)

women <- bind_rows(ir4e, ir5e) %>%
  mutate(
    row_id  = row_number(),
    weight  = v005 / 1e6,
    married = v502 == 1,
    ## Decision-making: 1 = she decides alone or jointly with husband/someone else
    decides_own_health   = has_say(v743a),
    decides_purchases    = has_say(v743b),
    decides_visits       = has_say(v743d),
    decides_husband_earn = has_say(v743f),
    ## Barriers: 1 = "big problem"; "not a big problem" and "no problem" are 0
    barrier_permission = big_problem(v467b),
    barrier_money      = big_problem(v467c),
    barrier_distance   = big_problem(v467d),
    barrier_alone      = big_problem(v467f),
    ## Education
    educ_years = if_else(v133 == 97, NA_real_, as.numeric(v133)),
    ## Water: on the premises or delivered = 0 minutes; not de jure resident or don't know = missing
    water_raw = case_when(v115 %in% c(0, 996)   ~ 0,
                          v115 %in% c(997, 998) ~ NA_real_,
                          TRUE                  ~ as.numeric(v115)),
    water_time_min_uncapped = water_raw,
    water_time_min          = pmin(water_raw, WATER_CAP),
    water_within30          = as.numeric(water_raw <= 30),
    improved_source = case_when(
      v113 == 97 | is.na(v113) ~ NA_real_,
      survey_round == "nfhs4"  ~ as.numeric(v113 %in% IMPROVED_WATER$nfhs4),
      TRUE                     ~ as.numeric(v113 %in% IMPROVED_WATER$nfhs5)),
    water_basic_jmp = as.numeric(improved_source == 1 & water_raw <= 30))

DECISION_ITEMS <- c("decides_own_health", "decides_purchases", "decides_visits", "decides_husband_earn")
BARRIER_ITEMS  <- c("barrier_permission", "barrier_money", "barrier_distance", "barrier_alone")

## Check 1: decision items exist only for married women in the state module, and the counts
## match the questionnaire design (86,811 and 76,910 married module women answered v743a).
outside <- women %>% filter(!(married & ssmod == 1))
stopifnot(all(is.na(as.matrix(outside[, DECISION_ITEMS]))))
stopifnot(sum(!is.na(ir4e$v743a)) == 86811, sum(!is.na(ir5e$v743a)) == 76910)

## Check 2: barrier items were asked of every woman.
stopifnot(all(!is.na(as.matrix(women[, BARRIER_ITEMS]))))

## Non-missing counts by round, for the methods section
women %>% group_by(survey_round) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(c(DECISION_ITEMS, BARRIER_ITEMS, "educ_years", "water_raw")),
                   ~ sum(!is.na(.x)))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-survey_round) %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey_round) %>% print(n = Inf)
```

## 6.3 Validate the water coding against the national reports

`v115` is a household question, so it is checked on the household file (`hv204`, same codes)
against the published household percentages: FR339 Table 2.1 (NFHS-4) and FR375 Table 2.1
(NFHS-5). The two reports cut time differently (NFHS-4: "less than 30 minutes"; NFHS-5:
"thirty minutes or less"), so each is checked on its own cut. Source codes are checked against each
report's own improved-source figure, and NFHS-5's "basic drinking water service" against FR375.

```{r s06-water-validate}
HR_WATER_VARS <- c("hv005", "hv201", "hv204", "hv236")
read_hr_water <- function(file, round_label) {
  read_dta(dhs_file(file), col_select = all_of(HR_WATER_VARS)) %>%
    zap_labels() %>% mutate(survey_round = round_label, w = hv005 / 1e6)
}
hrw <- bind_rows(
  checkpoint("hr4_water", HR_WATER_VARS, read_hr_water("IAHR74FL.DTA", "nfhs4")),
  checkpoint("hr5_water", HR_WATER_VARS, read_hr_water("IAHR7EFL.DTA", "nfhs5")))

wpct <- function(x, w) round(100 * sum(w[x]) / sum(w), 1)
val <- function(d, cut_lt) {
  premises <- d$hv204 %in% c(0, 996); dk <- d$hv204 == 998; t <- d$hv204
  near <- !premises & !dk & (if (cut_lt) t < 30 else t <= 30)
  far  <- !premises & !dk & (if (cut_lt) t >= 30 else t > 30)
  c(premises = wpct(premises, d$w), near = wpct(near, d$w), far = wpct(far, d$w), dont_know = wpct(dk, d$w))
}
h4 <- filter(hrw, survey_round == "nfhs4"); h5 <- filter(hrw, survey_round == "nfhs5")
off4 <- filter(h4, !hv204 %in% c(0, 996)); off5 <- filter(h5, !hv204 %in% c(0, 996))
basic5 <- h5$hv201 %in% IMPROVED_WATER$nfhs5 & (h5$hv204 %in% c(0, 996) | h5$hv204 <= 30)

water_validation <- tibble::tribble(
  ~indicator,                                   ~round,  ~ours,                                         ~official, ~source,
  "On premises or delivered (%)",               "NFHS-4", val(h4, TRUE)[["premises"]],                  66.3, "FR339 Table 2.1",
  "Less than 30 minutes (%)",                   "NFHS-4", val(h4, TRUE)[["near"]],                      27.2, "FR339 Table 2.1",
  "30 minutes or longer (%)",                   "NFHS-4", val(h4, TRUE)[["far"]],                        6.4, "FR339 Table 2.1",
  "Improved source, FR339 definition (%)",      "NFHS-4", wpct(h4$hv201 %in% IMPROVED_WATER_FR339, h4$w), 89.9, "FR339 Table 2.1",
  "Adult woman fetches water (%)",              "NFHS-4", wpct(off4$hv236 == 1, off4$w),                80.2, "FR339 Table 2.1",
  "On premises or delivered (%)",               "NFHS-5", val(h5, FALSE)[["premises"]],                 73.9, "FR375 Table 2.1",
  "Thirty minutes or less (%)",                 "NFHS-5", val(h5, FALSE)[["near"]],                     24.9, "FR375 Table 2.1",
  "More than 30 minutes (%)",                   "NFHS-5", val(h5, FALSE)[["far"]],                       1.2, "FR375 Table 2.1",
  "Improved source (%)",                        "NFHS-5", wpct(h5$hv201 %in% IMPROVED_WATER$nfhs5, h5$w), 95.9, "FR375 Table 2.1",
  "Basic drinking water service (%)",           "NFHS-5", wpct(basic5, h5$w),                           94.9, "FR375 Table 2.1",
  "Adult woman fetches water (%)",              "NFHS-5", wpct(off5$hv236 == 1, off5$w),                70.5, "FR375 Table 2.1") %>%
  mutate(diff = round(ours - official, 1))
print(water_validation, n = Inf)
stopifnot(all(abs(water_validation$diff) <= 0.2))
```

## 6.4 Build the two indices

```{r s06-pca}
## Pooled PCA on the women who answered all four items. Unweighted, on the correlation matrix,
## as in Ewerling et al. The first component is the index. Steps:
##   1. orient it so every loading is positive (higher score = more of each item);
##   2. divide by its pooled SD, so 1 unit = 1 SD (the raw score's SD is sqrt of the eigenvalue);
##   3. check the pooled formula against a PCA run on each round alone.
pooled_index <- function(df, items, label) {
  cc <- df %>% filter(if_all(all_of(items), ~ !is.na(.x)))
  p  <- prcomp(as.matrix(cc[, items]), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
  sgn   <- if (sum(p$rotation[, 1]) < 0) -1 else 1
  load  <- sgn * p$rotation[, 1]
  score <- sgn * p$x[, 1]
  stopifnot(all(load > 0))                     # every item points the same way
  own_round_r <- sapply(c("nfhs4", "nfhs5"), function(r) {
    k <- cc$survey_round == r
    abs(cor(prcomp(as.matrix(cc[k, items]), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)$x[, 1], score[k]))
  })
  ev <- p$sdev^2
  cat("\n---", label, "---\n",
      "Women used:", nrow(cc), "(NFHS-4", sum(cc$survey_round == "nfhs4"), "| NFHS-5", sum(cc$survey_round == "nfhs5"), ")\n",
      "Eigenvalues 1-2:", round(ev[1], 2), round(ev[2], 2),
      "| PC1 share of variance:", round(100 * ev[1] / sum(ev), 1), "%\n",
      "Raw PC1 SD (= sqrt eigenvalue):", round(sd(score), 3), "-> index divided by this\n",
      "Correlation of pooled score with own-round PCA score: NFHS-4", round(own_round_r[1], 3),
      "| NFHS-5", round(own_round_r[2], 3), "\n")
  items_table <- tibble(item = items, loading = round(load, 3),
                        mean = round(colMeans(cc[, items]), 3),
                        sd = round(apply(cc[, items], 2, sd), 3), n = nrow(cc))
  print(items_table)
  list(scores = tibble(row_id = cc$row_id, index = score / sd(score)), items = items_table,
       eigen = ev, own_round_r = own_round_r)
}
pca_decision <- pooled_index(women, DECISION_ITEMS, "Household decision-making index (higher = more say)")
pca_barrier  <- pooled_index(women, BARRIER_ITEMS,  "Healthcare access barrier index (higher = more barriers)")

women <- women %>%
  left_join(rename(pca_decision$scores, decision_index = index), by = "row_id") %>%
  left_join(rename(pca_barrier$scores,  barrier_index  = index), by = "row_id")
stopifnot(nrow(women) == 699686 + 724115)

write_csv(bind_rows(mutate(pca_decision$items, index = "decision"),
                    mutate(pca_barrier$items,  index = "barrier")),
          file.path(TABLE_DIR, "empowerment_pca_loadings.csv"))
```

## 6.4b Pre-treatment indices: NFHS-4 PCA weights (main), equal-weighted and Anderson

The pooled PCA above (6.4) learns its weights from both rounds. Because NFHS-5 answers can be
affected by the programme, the weights of the main index come from pre-treatment data only. This
chunk keeps 6.4 for comparison and adds three versions of each index, all built only from NFHS-4:

1. **Standardise** every item with its NFHS-4 mean and SD (all NFHS-4 women who answered all four
   items). The same means and SDs are applied to NFHS-5.
2. **NFHS-4 PCA** (`_n4`, the main index): PCA on the NFHS-4 standardised items; its loadings
   are applied unchanged to NFHS-5.
3. **Equal-weighted** (`_ew`, appendix): the plain average of the standardised items.
4. **Anderson (2008)** (`_and`, appendix): weights are the row sums of the inverse of the NFHS-4
   covariance matrix of the standardised items, so items that repeat each other's information get
   less weight (Schwab et al. 2020, steps 3 to 6).

Every version is rescaled to mean 0 and SD 1 among NFHS-4 women, so 1 unit = 1 SD of pre-treatment
women, and higher = more say (decision) or more barriers (barrier). Built unweighted on
the women who answered all four items, as the pooled PCA. A diagnostic table puts the weights side
by side, including a PCA run on NFHS-5 alone (only to see whether the weights moved; it is not used).

```{r s06-indices-alt}
alt_indices <- function(df, items, label, pooled) {
  cc  <- df %>% filter(if_all(all_of(items), ~ !is.na(.x)))
  X   <- as.matrix(cc[, items])
  ref <- cc$survey_round == "nfhs4"                       # reference group: all NFHS-4 women
  mu  <- colMeans(X[ref, ]); sdv <- apply(X[ref, ], 2, sd)
  Z   <- sweep(sweep(X, 2, mu), 2, sdv, "/")              # NFHS-4 standardisation, applied to both rounds
  rescale <- function(s) (s - mean(s[ref])) / sd(s[ref]) # mean 0, SD 1 among NFHS-4 women

  ## (1) PCA on NFHS-4 only (Z is already standardised on NFHS-4, so this is the NFHS-4 correlation PCA)
  p4   <- prcomp(Z[ref, ], center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)
  load4 <- p4$rotation[, 1] * if (sum(p4$rotation[, 1]) < 0) -1 else 1
  stopifnot(all(load4 > 0))
  s_n4 <- rescale(as.vector(Z %*% load4))

  ## (2) Equal-weighted mean of the standardised items
  s_ew <- rescale(rowMeans(Z))

  ## (3) Anderson: inverse-covariance weights from NFHS-4
  w_and <- rowSums(solve(cov(Z[ref, ])))
  s_and <- rescale(as.vector(Z %*% w_and) / sum(w_and))

  ## Diagnostic only: PCA on NFHS-5 alone, to see whether the weights differ by round
  p5    <- prcomp(X[!ref, ], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
  load5 <- p5$rotation[, 1] * if (sum(p5$rotation[, 1]) < 0) -1 else 1
  ev4   <- p4$sdev^2

  weights <- tibble(index = label, item = items,
                    nfhs4_mean = mu, nfhs4_sd = sdv,
                    pca_pooled = pooled$items$loading, pca_nfhs4 = unname(load4),
                    pca_nfhs5_only = unname(load5),
                    equal = 1 / length(items), anderson = unname(w_and / sum(w_and)))
  cat("\n---", label, "---\n",
      "Women: NFHS-4", sum(ref), "| NFHS-5", sum(!ref), "\n",
      "NFHS-4 PCA: first component explains", round(100 * ev4[1] / sum(ev4), 1), "% of variance\n")
  print(weights %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), width = Inf)

  scores <- tibble(row_id = cc$row_id, n4 = s_n4, ew = s_ew, and = s_and)
  ## How similar are the versions? Correlations with the pooled PCA index, all women
  pooled_score <- pooled$scores$index[match(cc$row_id, pooled$scores$row_id)]
  cors <- round(cor(cbind(pooled = pooled_score, n4 = s_n4, ew = s_ew, and = s_and)), 4)
  cat("Correlations between the four versions (all women):\n"); print(cors)
  list(scores = scores, weights = weights, cors = cors)
}
alt_decision <- alt_indices(women, DECISION_ITEMS, "decision", pca_decision)
alt_barrier  <- alt_indices(women, BARRIER_ITEMS,  "barrier",  pca_barrier)

women <- women %>%
  left_join(alt_decision$scores %>% rename(decision_index_n4 = n4, decision_index_ew = ew,
                                           decision_index_and = and), by = "row_id") %>%
  left_join(alt_barrier$scores %>% rename(barrier_index_n4 = n4, barrier_index_ew = ew,
                                          barrier_index_and = and), by = "row_id")
stopifnot(nrow(women) == 699686 + 724115)
## Same women as the pooled index: a version is missing exactly when the pooled index is
stopifnot(identical(is.na(women$decision_index), is.na(women$decision_index_n4)),
          identical(is.na(women$barrier_index),  is.na(women$barrier_index_n4)))

write_csv(bind_rows(alt_decision$weights, alt_barrier$weights),
          file.path(TABLE_DIR, "empowerment_index_weights_by_version.csv"))
```

## 6.4c PCA tables for the NFHS-4 index (main index)

The reporting tables for the PCA that sets the main index weights (6.4b): the PCA on
NFHS-4 women only, on the items standardised with NFHS-4 means and SDs, i.e. on the NFHS-4
correlation matrix. For each index, on the NFHS-4 women who answered all four items:

1. **Variance explained**: eigenvalue, share and cumulative share of variance for all four
   components. The index is the first component; the eigenvalue > 1 (Kaiser) rule and the share
   explained justify using one component.
2. **Loadings**: all four components, with each item's NFHS-4 mean and SD. Signs are oriented so
   every first-component loading is positive (higher index = more say / more barriers).
3. **Suitability for PCA**: Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin measure of sampling adequacy (overall and per item)
   and Bartlett's test that the correlation matrix is not an identity matrix. Computed in base R
   from the correlation matrix (KMO: squared correlations against squared partial correlations;
   Bartlett: $-(n - 1 - (2p+5)/6)\ln|R|$ with $p(p-1)/2$ df).
4. **Validation**: correlation of the main index with the pooled-PCA index (6.4), with the plain
   sum of the items, and, among NFHS-5 women, with a PCA estimated on NFHS-5 alone. High values
   mean the NFHS-4 weights rank women the same way as the alternatives.
5. **Index by round**: number of women, mean and SD of the main index in each round. By
   construction NFHS-4 has mean 0 and SD 1; the NFHS-5 mean is the change in NFHS-4 SD units
   (all India, all women with the items; not a treatment effect).

```{r s06-pca-n4-report}
kmo_bartlett <- function(X) {
  R <- cor(X); p <- ncol(R); n <- nrow(X)
  Q <- solve(R)
  A <- -Q / sqrt(outer(diag(Q), diag(Q)))                 # partial correlations
  off <- row(R) != col(R)
  r2 <- R^2 * off; a2 <- A^2 * off
  list(kmo = sum(r2) / (sum(r2) + sum(a2)),
       msa = rowSums(r2) / (rowSums(r2) + rowSums(a2)),
       chisq = -((n - 1) - (2 * p + 5) / 6) * log(det(R)),
       df = p * (p - 1) / 2)
}

pca_n4_report <- function(df, items, label, alt, pooled) {
  cc  <- df %>% filter(if_all(all_of(items), ~ !is.na(.x)))
  X   <- as.matrix(cc[, items]); ref <- cc$survey_round == "nfhs4"
  mu  <- colMeans(X[ref, ]); sdv <- apply(X[ref, ], 2, sd)
  Z   <- sweep(sweep(X, 2, mu), 2, sdv, "/")
  p4  <- prcomp(Z[ref, ], center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)  # identical to 6.4b
  sgn <- if (sum(p4$rotation[, 1]) < 0) -1 else 1
  rot <- p4$rotation; rot[, 1] <- sgn * rot[, 1]
  ev  <- p4$sdev^2
  ## Same weights as the index actually used (6.4b)
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(rot[, 1]), alt$weights$pca_nfhs4, tolerance = 1e-10)),
            abs(sum(ev) - length(items)) < 1e-8)

  variance <- tibble(index = label, component = paste0("PC", seq_along(ev)), eigenvalue = ev,
                     pct_variance = 100 * ev / sum(ev), cumulative_pct = cumsum(100 * ev / sum(ev)))
  loadings <- as_tibble(rot, rownames = "item") %>%
    mutate(index = label, nfhs4_mean = mu, nfhs4_sd = sdv, .before = 1)
  kb <- kmo_bartlett(X[ref, ])
  suitability <- bind_rows(
    tibble(index = label, statistic = "Women (NFHS-4, all four items)", item = NA_character_, value = sum(ref)),
    tibble(index = label, statistic = "Components with eigenvalue > 1", item = NA_character_, value = sum(ev > 1)),
    tibble(index = label, statistic = "KMO, overall", item = NA_character_, value = kb$kmo),
    tibble(index = label, statistic = "KMO, item", item = items, value = unname(kb$msa)),
    tibble(index = label, statistic = "Bartlett chi-square", item = NA_character_, value = kb$chisq),
    tibble(index = label, statistic = "Bartlett df", item = NA_character_, value = kb$df),
    tibble(index = label, statistic = "Bartlett p-value", item = NA_character_,
           value = pchisq(kb$chisq, kb$df, lower.tail = FALSE)))

  ## Validation correlations (main index = alt$scores$n4, same row order as cc)
  stopifnot(identical(alt$scores$row_id, cc$row_id))
  s_n4   <- alt$scores$n4
  s_pool <- pooled$scores$index[match(cc$row_id, pooled$scores$row_id)]
  p5     <- prcomp(X[!ref, ], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
  s5_own <- p5$x[, 1] * if (sum(p5$rotation[, 1]) < 0) -1 else 1
  validation <- tibble(index = label, comparison = c(
      "Pooled-PCA index (6.4), all women",
      "Sum of the four items, all women",
      "PCA on NFHS-5 alone, NFHS-5 women"),
    correlation = c(cor(s_n4, s_pool), cor(s_n4, rowSums(X)), cor(s_n4[!ref], s5_own)))
  by_round <- tibble(index = label, survey_round = cc$survey_round, s = s_n4) %>%
    group_by(index, survey_round) %>%
    summarise(women = n(), mean = mean(s), sd = sd(s), .groups = "drop")
  stopifnot(abs(by_round$mean[by_round$survey_round == "nfhs4"]) < 1e-8,
            abs(by_round$sd[by_round$survey_round == "nfhs4"] - 1) < 1e-8)

  cat("\n---", label, "(NFHS-4 PCA) ---\n"); print(variance %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))))
  print(loadings %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), width = Inf)
  cat("KMO", round(kb$kmo, 3), "| Bartlett chi2", round(kb$chisq, 1), "df", kb$df, "\n")
  print(validation %>% mutate(correlation = round(correlation, 4)))
  print(by_round %>% mutate(across(c(mean, sd), ~ round(.x, 3))))
  list(variance = variance, loadings = loadings, suitability = suitability,
       validation = validation, by_round = by_round)
}
rep_decision <- pca_n4_report(women, DECISION_ITEMS, "decision", alt_decision, pca_decision)
rep_barrier  <- pca_n4_report(women, BARRIER_ITEMS,  "barrier",  alt_barrier,  pca_barrier)

## Women behind the NFHS-4 PCA = the index samples in the sample-size table
stopifnot(rep_decision$by_round$women[rep_decision$by_round$survey_round == "nfhs4"] == 84860,
          rep_barrier$by_round$women[rep_barrier$by_round$survey_round == "nfhs4"] == 699686)

for (k in c("variance", "loadings", "suitability", "validation", "by_round"))
  write_csv(bind_rows(rep_decision[[k]], rep_barrier[[k]]), file.path(TABLE_DIR, paste0("pca_n4_", k, ".csv")))
cat("Saved pca_n4_variance/loadings/suitability/validation/by_round.csv\n")
```




## 6.5 Districts and the district panel

```{r s06-districts}
## Stage 05 sample: each kept district's NFHS-4 code (dist_id) and its NFHS-5 code.
nosplit <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_nosplit_map.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(in_sample)
ids <- bind_rows(
  nosplit %>% transmute(survey_round = "nfhs4", distcode, dist_id = distcode, adp_flag),
  ## dist_id must be set before distcode is overwritten: transmute() evaluates in order
  nosplit %>% transmute(survey_round = "nfhs5", dist_id = distcode, distcode = nfhs5_distcode, adp_flag))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ids[c("survey_round", "distcode")]),
          setequal(ids$dist_id[ids$survey_round == "nfhs4"], ids$dist_id[ids$survey_round == "nfhs5"]))

women_s <- women %>% inner_join(ids, by = c("survey_round", "distcode"))
cat("Women in the 582 districts: NFHS-4", sum(women_s$survey_round == "nfhs4"),
    "| NFHS-5", sum(women_s$survey_round == "nfhs5"), "\n")
stopifnot(all(count(distinct(women_s, survey_round, dist_id), survey_round)$n == 582))

## The two populations
POPULATIONS <- list(
  married_15_49 = quote(married & v012 >= 15 & v012 <= 49),
  women_15_24   = quote(v012 >= 15 & v012 <= 24))
OUTCOMES <- c("decision_index", "barrier_index", "educ_years", "water_time_min",
              "water_time_min_uncapped", "water_within30", "water_basic_jmp")

wmean <- function(x, w) { k <- !is.na(x); if (!any(k)) NA_real_ else sum(x[k] * w[k]) / sum(w[k]) }
collapse_pop <- function(pop) {
  women_s %>% filter(!!POPULATIONS[[pop]]) %>%
    group_by(dist_id, survey_round, adp_flag) %>%
    summarise(across(all_of(OUTCOMES), list(mean = ~ wmean(.x, weight), n = ~ sum(!is.na(.x))),
                     .names = "{.col}__{.fn}"), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(population = pop, .after = adp_flag)
}
empowerment_panel <- bind_rows(lapply(names(POPULATIONS), collapse_pop)) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("__mean$", "", .x)) %>% rename_with(~ sub("^(.*)__n$", "n_\\1", .x))

## Check: one row per district, round and population; no district without water or barrier data.
## Every district and population must have both rounds under the same dist_id.
pairs <- count(empowerment_panel, dist_id, population)
stopifnot(nrow(pairs) == 582 * 2, all(pairs$n == 2))
stopifnot(nrow(empowerment_panel) == 582 * 2 * 2,
          !anyNA(empowerment_panel$barrier_index), !anyNA(empowerment_panel$water_time_min))

## Women behind each district mean: minimum, median, and districts with fewer than 25.
cell_sizes <- empowerment_panel %>%
  select(population, survey_round, starts_with("n_")) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(starts_with("n_"), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "n") %>%
  group_by(population, outcome, survey_round) %>%
  summarise(min = min(n), median = median(n), districts_under_25 = sum(n < 25), .groups = "drop")
print(cell_sizes %>% filter(outcome %in% paste0("n_", c("decision_index", "barrier_index", "educ_years", "water_time_min"))), n = Inf)
cat("District-rounds with no decision-making data:",
    sum(is.na(empowerment_panel$decision_index)), "\n")

write_csv(empowerment_panel, file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_empowerment_nosplit.csv"))
write_csv(cell_sizes,        file.path(TABLE_DIR, "empowerment_cell_sizes.csv"))
```

## 6.5b District means of the pre-treatment indices

The six new index columns from 6.4b, averaged to district, round and population exactly as in 6.5
(same women, same survey weights). Saved to a separate file so the existing district panel is
unchanged. Each district mean rests on the same women as the pooled index, which is checked.

```{r s06-districts-alt}
ALT_INDICES <- c(paste0("decision_index_", c("n4", "ew", "and")),
                 paste0("barrier_index_",  c("n4", "ew", "and")))
empowerment_alt <- bind_rows(lapply(names(POPULATIONS), function(pop)
  women_s %>% filter(!!POPULATIONS[[pop]]) %>%
    group_by(dist_id, survey_round, adp_flag) %>%
    ## counts first: inside summarise(), a column already summarised would be counted as 1
    summarise(n_decision_alt = sum(!is.na(decision_index_n4)),
              n_barrier_alt  = sum(!is.na(barrier_index_n4)),
              across(all_of(ALT_INDICES), ~ wmean(.x, weight)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(population = pop, .after = adp_flag)))

## Checks: every district has both rounds; women behind each mean = women behind the pooled index
pairs_alt <- count(empowerment_alt, dist_id, population)
stopifnot(nrow(pairs_alt) == 582 * 2, all(pairs_alt$n == 2))
chk_alt <- empowerment_alt %>%
  inner_join(empowerment_panel %>% select(dist_id, survey_round, population, n_decision_index, n_barrier_index),
             by = c("dist_id", "survey_round", "population"))
stopifnot(nrow(chk_alt) == nrow(empowerment_alt),
          all(chk_alt$n_decision_alt == chk_alt$n_decision_index),
          all(chk_alt$n_barrier_alt == chk_alt$n_barrier_index))

write_csv(empowerment_alt %>% select(-n_decision_alt, -n_barrier_alt),
          file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_empowerment_alt_indices.csv"))
cat("Saved district_empowerment_alt_indices.csv:", nrow(empowerment_alt), "rows\n")
```

## 6.5c Sample sizes: one table for every empowerment N

Every number of women used anywhere in the empowerment analysis, from all interviewed women down
to each outcome and population in the 582 sample districts, with its definition. Counts are
unweighted numbers of women, NFHS-4 and NFHS-5. Reading down a block explains each drop: for
example, the decision-making questions are asked only of currently married women in the state
module, and "husband's earnings" is missing when the husband has no earnings, which is why fewer
women answer all four items than answer the first one.

```{r s06-sample-sizes}
n_by_round <- function(d) c(nfhs4 = sum(d$survey_round == "nfhs4"), nfhs5 = sum(d$survey_round == "nfhs5"))
n_row <- function(block, step, definition, d) {
  n <- n_by_round(d)
  tibble(block = block, step = step, definition = definition, nfhs4 = n[["nfhs4"]], nfhs5 = n[["nfhs5"]])
}
all_dec <- women %>% filter(if_all(all_of(DECISION_ITEMS), ~ !is.na(.x)))
all_bar <- women %>% filter(if_all(all_of(BARRIER_ITEMS),  ~ !is.na(.x)))
in_pop  <- function(d, pop) d %>% filter(!!POPULATIONS[[pop]])

sample_sizes <- bind_rows(
  n_row("All women", "Interviewed women", "Every woman in the women's file (FR339 / FR375 totals)", women),
  n_row("All women", "In the 582 sample districts", "Districts with the same boundaries in both rounds (Stage 05)", women_s),

  n_row("Decision-making", "Eligible", "Currently married and in a state-module household", women %>% filter(married, ssmod == 1)),
  bind_rows(lapply(DECISION_ITEMS, function(it)
    n_row("Decision-making", paste("Answered:", it), "Valid answer to this item (all India)", women %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[it]]))))),
  n_row("Decision-making", "Answered all four items", "Index sample: PCA, NFHS-4 weights, equal-weighted and Anderson (all India)", all_dec),
  n_row("Decision-making", "... in the 582 districts", "Index sample in the sample districts", all_dec %>% semi_join(women_s, by = "row_id")),
  n_row("Decision-making", "... married women 15-49", "Estimation population: married women aged 15-49", in_pop(women_s, "married_15_49") %>% filter(!is.na(decision_index))),
  n_row("Decision-making", "... women 15-24", "Estimation population: women aged 15-24 (all of them married, as the items require)", in_pop(women_s, "women_15_24") %>% filter(!is.na(decision_index))),

  n_row("Barriers", "Answered all four items", "Asked of every woman (all India)", all_bar),
  n_row("Barriers", "... married women 15-49", "Estimation population in the 582 districts", in_pop(women_s, "married_15_49") %>% filter(!is.na(barrier_index))),
  n_row("Barriers", "... women 15-24", "Estimation population in the 582 districts", in_pop(women_s, "women_15_24") %>% filter(!is.na(barrier_index))),

  n_row("Education", "... women 15-24", "Years of education known (v133 not 97), 582 districts", in_pop(women_s, "women_15_24") %>% filter(!is.na(educ_years))),

  n_row("Water", "... married women 15-49", "Water time known (not 997/998), 582 districts", in_pop(women_s, "married_15_49") %>% filter(!is.na(water_time_min))),
  n_row("Water", "... women 15-24", "Water time known (not 997/998), 582 districts", in_pop(women_s, "women_15_24") %>% filter(!is.na(water_time_min)))
) %>% mutate(total = nfhs4 + nfhs5)

print(sample_sizes, n = Inf, width = Inf)

## Checks: the counts that appear elsewhere in the pipeline
stopifnot(sample_sizes$nfhs4[1] == 699686, sample_sizes$nfhs5[1] == 724115,
          sum(!is.na(ir4e$v743a)) == sample_sizes$nfhs4[sample_sizes$step == "Answered: decides_own_health"],
          nrow(all_dec) == nrow(alt_decision$scores))
## The district panel's women counts add up to the estimation populations above
for (pop in names(POPULATIONS)) for (v in c("decision_index", "barrier_index")) {
  blk <- if (v == "decision_index") "Decision-making" else "Barriers"
  stp <- if (pop == "married_15_49") "... married women 15-49" else "... women 15-24"
  r <- sample_sizes %>% filter(block == blk, step == stp)
  p <- empowerment_panel %>% filter(population == pop)
  stopifnot(sum(p[[paste0("n_", v)]][p$survey_round == "nfhs4"]) == r$nfhs4,
            sum(p[[paste0("n_", v)]][p$survey_round == "nfhs5"]) == r$nfhs5)
}
write_csv(sample_sizes, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "empowerment_sample_sizes.csv"))
```

## 6.6 Appendix: water collection time diagnostics

Three checks for the appendix: how many women report more than 120 minutes and what
they report; how much the cap moves district means and the raw difference-in-differences; and how
much the 30-minute cut depends on answers of exactly 30 (heaping). The last part shows who fetches
water in households without water on the premises, by AD status.

```{r s06-water-diagnostics}
## (a) Reports above the cap, all women
over <- women %>% filter(water_raw > WATER_CAP)
cat("Women reporting more than", WATER_CAP, "minutes: NFHS-4", sum(over$survey_round == "nfhs4"),
    "of", sum(women$survey_round == "nfhs4"), "| NFHS-5", sum(over$survey_round == "nfhs5"),
    "of", sum(women$survey_round == "nfhs5"), "\n")
print(over %>% count(survey_round, minutes = water_raw) %>%
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey_round, values_from = n, values_fill = 0), n = Inf)

## (b) Effect of the cap on district means (married women 15-49) and on the raw DiD
m <- empowerment_panel %>% filter(population == "married_15_49")
cap_effect <- m %>% mutate(change = water_time_min_uncapped - water_time_min)
cat("Change in district mean from capping (minutes): mean", round(mean(cap_effect$change), 3),
    "| 99th percentile", round(quantile(cap_effect$change, 0.99), 2),
    "| max", round(max(cap_effect$change), 2),
    "| correlation", round(cor(m$water_time_min, m$water_time_min_uncapped), 4), "\n")
raw_did <- function(v) {
  g <- m %>% group_by(adp_flag, survey_round) %>% summarise(y = mean(.data[[v]]), .groups = "drop")
  y <- function(a, r) g$y[g$adp_flag == a & g$survey_round == r]
  (y(1, "nfhs5") - y(1, "nfhs4")) - (y(0, "nfhs5") - y(0, "nfhs4"))
}
women_drop <- women_s %>% filter(married) %>%
  mutate(w_drop = if_else(water_raw > WATER_CAP, NA_real_, water_raw)) %>%
  group_by(dist_id, survey_round, adp_flag) %>%
  summarise(water_dropped = wmean(w_drop, weight), .groups = "drop")
m <- m %>% left_join(women_drop, by = c("dist_id", "survey_round", "adp_flag"))
cap_did <- tibble(version = c("uncapped", paste0("capped at ", WATER_CAP), paste0("above ", WATER_CAP, " dropped")),
                  raw_did = round(c(raw_did("water_time_min_uncapped"), raw_did("water_time_min"),
                                    raw_did("water_dropped")), 3))
print(cap_did)

## (c) Heaping at 30 minutes, among women who fetch water off the premises
heap <- women %>% filter(water_raw > 0) %>% group_by(survey_round) %>%
  summarise(off_premises = n(), exactly_30_pct = round(100 * mean(water_raw == 30), 1),
            under_30_pct = round(100 * mean(water_raw < 30), 1),
            at_most_30_pct = round(100 * mean(water_raw <= 30), 1))
print(heap)

## (d) Who fetches water (households without water on the premises), by AD status, 582 districts
hr_ids <- function(file, distvar, round_label) {
  read_dta(dhs_file(file), col_select = all_of(c("hv005", "hv204", "hv236", distvar))) %>%
    zap_labels() %>% mutate(distcode = as.numeric(.data[[distvar]]), survey_round = round_label)
}
who_fetches <- bind_rows(
  checkpoint("hr4_fetch", c(HR_WATER_VARS, "shdistri"), hr_ids("IAHR74FL.DTA", "shdistri", "nfhs4")),
  checkpoint("hr5_fetch", c(HR_WATER_VARS, "shdist"),   hr_ids("IAHR7EFL.DTA", "shdist",   "nfhs5"))) %>%
  filter(!hv204 %in% c(0, 996), !is.na(hv236)) %>%
  inner_join(ids, by = c("survey_round", "distcode")) %>%
  group_by(survey_round, group = if_else(adp_flag == 1, "AD", "Non-AD")) %>%
  summarise(households = n(),
            adult_woman_pct = round(100 * sum((hv236 == 1) * hv005) / sum(hv005), 1),
            girl_under15_pct = round(100 * sum((hv236 == 3) * hv005) / sum(hv005), 1),
            .groups = "drop")
print(who_fetches)

## (e) Figures
suppressPackageStartupMessages(suppressWarnings({ library(ggplot2) }))   # hide 'built under R x.y' notices
th <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank())
fig_a <- ggplot(women %>% filter(water_raw > 0) %>%
                  mutate(round = recode(survey_round, nfhs4 = "NFHS-4", nfhs5 = "NFHS-5")),
                aes(x = pmin(water_raw, 900))) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, boundary = 0, fill = "#2a78d6", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = WATER_CAP, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_sqrt(labels = scales::comma) + facet_wrap(~ round, ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "Reported round-trip time, women who fetch water off the premises",
       subtitle = "Dashed line: 120-minute cap. Square-root count scale.",
       x = "Minutes (one trip: go, get water, come back)", y = "Women") + th
fig_b <- ggplot(m %>% mutate(group = if_else(adp_flag == 1, "AD", "Non-AD"),
                             round = recode(survey_round, nfhs4 = "NFHS-4", nfhs5 = "NFHS-5")),
                aes(x = water_time_min_uncapped, y = water_time_min, colour = group)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(size = 1.4, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("AD" = "#eb6834", "Non-AD" = "#2a78d6")) +
  facet_wrap(~ round, ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "District mean water time, married women 15-49",
       subtitle = "Uncapped vs capped at 120 minutes; 582 districts per round",
       x = "Uncapped mean (minutes)", y = "Capped mean (minutes)") + th
ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, "appendix_water_time_distribution.png"), fig_a, width = 6, height = 6, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, "appendix_water_cap_district_means.png"), fig_b, width = 6, height = 6, dpi = 200, bg = "white")

write_csv(cap_did,     file.path(TABLE_DIR, "appendix_water_cap_did.csv"))
write_csv(heap,        file.path(TABLE_DIR, "appendix_water_heaping_30.csv"))
write_csv(who_fetches, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "appendix_water_who_fetches.csv"))
```


# Stage 07: Descriptive statistics

Descriptive statistics for the estimation samples, before any matching:

1. **Sample flow** from 640 NFHS-4 districts to the estimation samples (7.1).
2. **Health outcomes by AD status** in each round, as in A&M Table 2 (7.2).
3. **Covariate balance before matching**, as in A&M Table 3 (7.3).
4. **Baseline covariates** by AD status: N, mean, SD, min, max (thesis Table 5) (7.4).
5. **Empowerment outcomes, women**: items, indices, education and water by round, for all women and
   by AD status (thesis Table 6) (7.5).
6. **Empowerment outcomes, districts**: district means by AD status and round (7.6).
7. **Dropped districts** compared with the kept sample (7.7).
8. **Pre-COVID** versions of 2 and 3 (7.8).

Unless stated otherwise, district-level statistics weight every district equally, as the DiD does.
Women-level statistics use the women's weight `v005`; N is the unweighted number of women.
Tables are saved to `outputs/tables/` with the prefix `desc_`.

```{r s07-setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(suppressWarnings({ library(MatchIt) }))   # hide 'built under R x.y' notices

## NFHS-5 Phase 1 (pre-COVID) States/UTs, verified against PIB PRID=1680702,
## written as they appear in NFHS-4 (Ladakh was part of Jammu and Kashmir; Dadra and Nagar Haveli
## and Daman and Diu were separate UTs).
PHASE1_STATES_NFHS4 <- c("andhra pradesh", "assam", "bihar", "goa", "gujarat", "himachal pradesh",
  "karnataka", "kerala", "maharashtra", "manipur", "meghalaya", "mizoram", "nagaland", "sikkim",
  "telangana", "tripura", "west bengal", "andaman and nicobar islands", "dadra and nagar haveli",
  "daman and diu", "jammu and kashmir", "lakshadweep")

baseline   <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_baseline_nosplit.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
panel      <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_panel_nosplit.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
emp_panel  <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_empowerment_nosplit.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
nosplit    <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_nosplit_map.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
base_full  <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_baseline_full.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

baseline <- baseline %>% mutate(precovid = state_name %in% PHASE1_STATES_NFHS4)
psm_full     <- baseline %>% filter(if_all(all_of(names(COVARIATES)), ~ !is.na(.x)))
psm_precovid <- psm_full %>% filter(precovid)
stopifnot(all(PHASE1_STATES_NFHS4 %in% base_full$state_name))   # every name matches an NFHS-4 state
```

## 7.1 Sample flow

```{r s07-flow}
flow_row <- function(step, d) tibble(step = step, districts = nrow(d),
                                     ad = sum(d$adp_flag == 1), non_ad = sum(d$adp_flag == 0))
sample_flow <- bind_rows(
  flow_row("NFHS-4 districts (2011 boundaries)",                    base_full),
  flow_row("Same boundaries in both rounds (NOSPLIT, Stage 05)",     baseline),
  flow_row("All 12 matching covariates available (full sample)",     psm_full),
  flow_row("Pre-COVID: NFHS-5 Phase 1 States/UTs (pre-COVID sample)", psm_precovid))
print(sample_flow)

    "| at step 3:", nrow(baseline) - nrow(psm_full), "with a missing covariate\n")

stopifnot(nrow(baseline) == 582, nrow(psm_full) == 570, sum(psm_full$adp_flag) == 102)
write_csv(sample_flow, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "desc_sample_flow.csv"))
```

## 7.2 Health outcomes by AD status (A&M Table 2)

District means, AD and non-AD, in each round, with the p-value of a Welch two-sample t-test
(unequal variances). A&M do not state which test they used.

```{r s07-health}
health_table <- function(pnl, sample_label) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("nfhs4", "nfhs5"), function(r) {
    d <- pnl %>% filter(survey_round == r)
    bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(HEALTH_OUTCOMES)), function(i) {
      v <- HEALTH_OUTCOMES$var[i]; x <- d[[v]]
      ad <- x[d$adp_flag == 1]; nad <- x[d$adp_flag == 0]
      tibble(no = HEALTH_OUTCOMES$no[i], indicator = HEALTH_OUTCOMES$label[i], round = r,
             n_non_ad = sum(!is.na(nad)), mean_non_ad = mean(nad, na.rm = TRUE),
             n_ad = sum(!is.na(ad)), mean_ad = mean(ad, na.rm = TRUE),
             p_value = t.test(nad, ad)$p.value)
    }))
  })) %>% mutate(sample = sample_label)
}
table2_full <- health_table(panel, "full (582 districts)")
print(table2_full %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
        select(no, round, n_non_ad, mean_non_ad, n_ad, mean_ad, p_value), n = Inf)
write_csv(table2_full, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "desc_table2_health_outcomes_full.csv"))
```

## 7.3 Covariate balance before matching (A&M Table 3)

Computed with `MatchIt` without matching (`method = NULL`), so the statistics are defined exactly as
in the after-matching tables of the next stage: standardised mean difference (estimand ATT, so the
difference is divided by the AD standard deviation), variance ratio, and eCDF mean and maximum.

```{r s07-balance}
balance_before <- function(d, sample_label) {
  f <- as.formula(paste("adp_flag ~", paste(names(COVARIATES), collapse = " + ")))
  s <- summary(matchit(f, data = d, method = NULL, distance = "glm", estimand = "ATT"))$sum.all
  as.data.frame(s) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("var") %>% filter(var %in% names(COVARIATES)) %>%
    transmute(covariate = COVARIATES[var], mean_ad = `Means Treated`, mean_non_ad = `Means Control`,
              std_mean_diff = `Std. Mean Diff.`, var_ratio = `Var. Ratio`,
              ecdf_mean = `eCDF Mean`, ecdf_max = `eCDF Max`, sample = sample_label,
              n_ad = sum(d$adp_flag == 1), n_non_ad = sum(d$adp_flag == 0)) %>%
    tibble::as_tibble()
}
table3_full <- balance_before(psm_full, "full (570 districts)")
print(table3_full %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), n = Inf)
cat("Covariates with |SMD| < 0.10:", sum(abs(table3_full$std_mean_diff) < 0.10),
    "| < 0.25:", sum(abs(table3_full$std_mean_diff) < 0.25), "of 12\n")
write_csv(table3_full, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "desc_table3_balance_before_full.csv"))
```

## 7.4 Baseline covariates by AD status (thesis Table 5)

```{r s07-covariates}
describe_by_ad <- function(d) {
  d %>% select(adp_flag, all_of(names(COVARIATES))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-adp_flag, names_to = "var") %>%
    group_by(group = if_else(adp_flag == 1, "AD", "Non-AD"), var) %>%
    summarise(N = sum(!is.na(value)), mean = mean(value), sd = sd(value),
              min = min(value), max = max(value), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(covariate = COVARIATES[var], .before = 1) %>% select(-var) %>%
    arrange(match(covariate, COVARIATES), desc(group))
}
table5 <- describe_by_ad(psm_full)
print(table5 %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))), n = Inf)
write_csv(table5, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "desc_table5_covariates_by_ad.csv"))
```

### Table 5 with t-tests

The matching covariates by AD status with the difference in means and a Welch two-sample t-test
(unequal variances; the same test as Table 2 above), one row per covariate, for both samples.
These are the covariates used in the propensity score, measured before the programme (NFHS-4 and
the sources in Stage 03).

```{r s07-covariates-ttest}
ttest_table <- function(d, sample_label) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(COVARIATES), function(v) {
    ad <- d[[v]][d$adp_flag == 1]; nad <- d[[v]][d$adp_flag == 0]
    tt <- t.test(ad, nad)
    tibble(sample = sample_label, covariate = COVARIATES[[v]],
           n_ad = length(ad), mean_ad = mean(ad), sd_ad = sd(ad),
           n_non_ad = length(nad), mean_non_ad = mean(nad), sd_non_ad = sd(nad),
           difference = mean(ad) - mean(nad), t_stat = unname(tt$statistic), p_value = tt$p.value)
  }))
}
table5_ttest <- bind_rows(ttest_table(psm_full, "full"), ttest_table(psm_precovid, "precovid"))
print(table5_ttest %>% select(sample, covariate, mean_ad, mean_non_ad, difference, t_stat, p_value) %>%
        mutate(across(c(mean_ad, mean_non_ad, difference, t_stat), ~ round(.x, 2)),
               p_value = signif(p_value, 3)), n = Inf, width = Inf)
write_csv(table5_ttest, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "desc_table5_covariates_ttest.csv"))
```

## 7.5 Empowerment outcomes, women (thesis Table 6)

Uses the woman-level data built in Stage 06 (`women_s`: women in the 582 districts). N is the
unweighted number of women; means and SDs use `v005`. Each item and outcome uses the women who
answered it. Water time is capped at 120 minutes; the uncapped maximum is printed for the table note.

```{r s07-women}
if (!exists("women_s")) stop("Run Stage 06 first in this session: it creates women_s.")
## Use the main index (PCA weights from NFHS-4, Stage 6.4b) in the descriptive tables, so they
## describe the same index as the results.
women_d <- women_s %>% mutate(decision_index = decision_index_n4, barrier_index = barrier_index_n4)

T6_ROWS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~var,                    ~label,                                          ~block,
  "decision_index",        "Household decision-making index (SD units)",    "Household decision-making (1 = she has a say)",
  "decides_own_health",    "Own health care",                               "Household decision-making (1 = she has a say)",
  "decides_purchases",     "Large household purchases",                     "Household decision-making (1 = she has a say)",
  "decides_visits",        "Visits to family or relatives",                 "Household decision-making (1 = she has a say)",
  "decides_husband_earn",  "Use of husband's/partner's earnings",           "Household decision-making (1 = she has a say)",
  "barrier_index",         "Healthcare access barrier index (SD units)",    "Healthcare access barriers (1 = big problem)",
  "barrier_permission",    "Needing permission to go",                      "Healthcare access barriers (1 = big problem)",
  "barrier_money",         "Getting money needed for treatment",            "Healthcare access barriers (1 = big problem)",
  "barrier_distance",      "Distance to health facility",                   "Healthcare access barriers (1 = big problem)",
  "barrier_alone",         "Not wanting to go alone",                       "Healthcare access barriers (1 = big problem)",
  "educ_years",            "Woman's education (years)",                     "Education",
  "water_time_min",        "Round-trip time to water source (minutes, capped at 120)", "Time use",
  "water_within30",        "Collection time within 30 minutes (JMP time criterion)",   "Time use")
T6_POP <- list(married_15_49 = setdiff(T6_ROWS$var, "educ_years"), women_15_24 = T6_ROWS$var)

wsd <- function(x, w) { m <- sum(x * w) / sum(w); sqrt(sum(w * (x - m)^2) / sum(w)) }
women_table <- function(d, pop) {
  d <- d %>% filter(!!POPULATIONS[[pop]])
  bind_rows(lapply(T6_POP[[pop]], function(v) {
    d %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[v]])) %>%
      group_by(survey_round) %>%
      summarise(N = n(), mean = sum(.data[[v]] * weight) / sum(weight), sd = wsd(.data[[v]], weight),
                min = min(.data[[v]]), max = max(.data[[v]]), .groups = "drop") %>%
      mutate(var = v)
  })) %>% mutate(population = pop)
}
table6 <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(T6_POP), function(p) mutate(women_table(women_d, p), group = "All")),
  lapply(names(T6_POP), function(p) mutate(women_table(filter(women_d, adp_flag == 1), p), group = "AD")),
  lapply(names(T6_POP), function(p) mutate(women_table(filter(women_d, adp_flag == 0), p), group = "Non-AD"))) %>%
  left_join(T6_ROWS, by = "var") %>%
  select(population, group, block, label, survey_round, N, mean, sd, min, max)

print(table6 %>% filter(group == "All") %>% mutate(across(c(mean, sd), ~ round(.x, 2))), n = Inf)
cat("Water time before the cap, maximum (minutes): NFHS-4",
    max(women_s$water_time_min_uncapped[women_s$survey_round == "nfhs4"], na.rm = TRUE),
    "| NFHS-5", max(women_s$water_time_min_uncapped[women_s$survey_round == "nfhs5"], na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
write_csv(table6, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "desc_table6_empowerment_women.csv"))
```


# Stage 08: Propensity-score matching

Matching on the 12 baseline covariates, as in A&M: a logit propensity score, full matching for the
ATT, and nearest-neighbour and genetic matching at 3:1 ("For both methods, we implement matching
for 3:1 control versus treatment units", A&M Section 4.3).

**Specifications:**

| Spec | Method | Common support | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full` | Full matching | none: all districts kept | **Main result** |
| `full_cs` | Full matching | `discard = "both"`: districts outside the overlap of AD and non-AD propensity scores dropped | Robustness (A&M-style common support) |
| `nearest` | Nearest neighbour, 3 controls per AD, without replacement | none | Robustness |
| `genetic` | Genetic matching, 3 controls per AD, without replacement | none | Robustness |

Each is run on the full sample (570 districts) and the pre-COVID sample (260). The main result keeps
all ADs, so the effect is for all 102 ADs (40 pre-COVID). A&M imposed common support, so `full_cs` is
the A&M-style check.

**Balance criterion:** abs(SMD) < 0.10 counts as balanced; > 0.25 is serious imbalance.

**Effective sample size (ESS)** of the matched controls is reported for every specification. A low
ESS means the weights rest on a few non-AD districts, which makes the DiD fragile.

Needs the packages `optmatch` (full matching) and `Matching` and `rgenoud` (genetic matching).

```{r s08-setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(suppressWarnings({ library(MatchIt); library(ggplot2) }))   # hide 'built under R x.y' notices
missing_pkgs <- c("optmatch", "Matching", "rgenoud")[!sapply(c("optmatch", "Matching", "rgenoud"), requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_pkgs)) stop("Install first: install.packages(c(\"", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = "\", \""), "\"))")

## Same samples as Stage 07 (rebuilt here so this stage can run on its own)
COVARIATES <- c(
  pct_landless_manual_labor = "Landless household dependent on manual labour",
  pct_anc_first_trimester   = "Antenatal check-up in the first trimester",
  pct_anc_4plus_visits      = "At least 4 antenatal care visits",
  pct_full_anc              = "Full antenatal care",
  pct_institutional_birth   = "Institutional births",
  pct_stunted               = "Stunted children (<5 years)",
  pct_wasted                = "Wasted children (<5 years)",
  pct_severely_wasted       = "Severely wasted children (<5 years)",
  pct_adverse_ptr           = "Adverse pupil-teacher ratio",
  pct_unelectrified         = "Unelectrified household",
  pct_no_individual_toilet  = "Household without individual toilet",
  pct_no_water_access       = "Household without access to water")
PHASE1_STATES_NFHS4 <- c("andhra pradesh", "assam", "bihar", "goa", "gujarat", "himachal pradesh",
  "karnataka", "kerala", "maharashtra", "manipur", "meghalaya", "mizoram", "nagaland", "sikkim",
  "telangana", "tripura", "west bengal", "andaman and nicobar islands", "dadra and nagar haveli",
  "daman and diu", "jammu and kashmir", "lakshadweep")

psm_full <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_baseline_nosplit.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(if_all(all_of(names(COVARIATES)), ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
  select(dist_id, district_name, state_name, adp_flag, all_of(names(COVARIATES))) %>%
  as.data.frame()
psm_precovid <- psm_full %>% filter(state_name %in% PHASE1_STATES_NFHS4)
stopifnot(nrow(psm_full) == 570, sum(psm_full$adp_flag) == 102,
          nrow(psm_precovid) == 260, sum(psm_precovid$adp_flag) == 40)

PS_FORMULA <- as.formula(paste("adp_flag ~", paste(names(COVARIATES), collapse = " + ")))
SMD_BALANCED <- 0.10; SMD_SERIOUS <- 0.25
GENETIC_POP_SIZE <- 500   # GenMatch population size, set explicitly for reproducibility

SPECS <- list(
  full     = list(method = "full"),
  full_cs  = list(method = "full", discard = "both"),
  nearest  = list(method = "nearest", ratio = 3, replace = FALSE),
  genetic  = list(method = "genetic", ratio = 3, replace = FALSE, pop.size = GENETIC_POP_SIZE))
```

## 8.1 Run the matching

```{r s08-match}
run_spec <- function(d, spec_name) {
  args <- c(list(formula = PS_FORMULA, data = d, distance = "glm", estimand = "ATT"), SPECS[[spec_name]])
  set.seed(SEED)
  m <- do.call(matchit, args)
  md <- match.data(m)   # districts that are matched (discarded or unmatched ones are dropped)
  list(m = m, md = md)
}
SAMPLES <- list(full = psm_full, precovid = psm_precovid)
matches <- list()
for (s in names(SAMPLES)) for (sp in names(SPECS)) {
  key <- paste(s, sp, sep = "__")
  message("Matching: ", key)
  matches[[key]] <- checkpoint(paste0("match_", key), list(SPECS[[sp]], SEED, SAMPLES[[s]]$dist_id),
                               run_spec(SAMPLES[[s]], sp))
}
```

## 8.2 Balance after matching and the summary table

For each specification: the after-matching balance table in A&M's format (their Tables 4, 7, 9 and
10), and one summary row like the progress report's Table 3, with the matched counts and the ESS.

```{r s08-balance}
balance_table <- function(m, which = c("sum.matched", "sum.all")) {
  s <- summary(m)[[match.arg(which)]]
  as.data.frame(s) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("var") %>% filter(var %in% names(COVARIATES)) %>%
    transmute(var, covariate = COVARIATES[var], mean_ad = `Means Treated`, mean_non_ad = `Means Control`,
              std_mean_diff = `Std. Mean Diff.`, var_ratio = `Var. Ratio`,
              ecdf_mean = `eCDF Mean`, ecdf_max = `eCDF Max`) %>% tibble::as_tibble()
}
balance_after <- bind_rows(lapply(names(matches), function(k) {
  balance_table(matches[[k]]$m) %>% mutate(sample = sub("__.*", "", k), spec = sub(".*__", "", k))
}))

matching_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(matches), function(k) {
  m <- matches[[k]]$m; md <- matches[[k]]$md; d <- SAMPLES[[sub("__.*", "", k)]]
  b <- balance_table(m); a <- abs(b$std_mean_diff)
  nn <- summary(m)$nn
  tibble(sample = sub("__.*", "", k), spec = sub(".*__", "", k),
         ad_matched = sum(md$adp_flag == 1), ad_total = sum(d$adp_flag == 1),
         non_ad_matched = sum(md$adp_flag == 0), non_ad_total = sum(d$adp_flag == 0),
         ess_controls = round(nn["Matched (ESS)", "Control"], 1),
         balanced_010 = sum(a < SMD_BALANCED), below_025 = sum(a < SMD_SERIOUS),
         worst_covariate = b$covariate[which.max(a)], max_abs_smd = round(max(a), 3))
}))
print(matching_summary, width = Inf)

## Checks: the main spec keeps every district; common support drops units from both groups.
main <- matching_summary %>% filter(spec == "full")
stopifnot(all(main$ad_matched == main$ad_total), all(main$non_ad_matched == main$non_ad_total))

print(balance_after %>% filter(spec == "full") %>% select(sample, covariate, std_mean_diff, var_ratio, ecdf_max) %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), n = Inf)

write_csv(matching_summary, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "match_summary.csv"))
write_csv(balance_after,    file.path(TABLE_DIR, "match_balance_after.csv"))
```

## 8.3 Figures: balance before and after, and covariate densities

```{r s08-figures}
## (a) Absolute SMD for every covariate: before matching and after each specification
before <- bind_rows(lapply(names(SAMPLES), function(s)
  balance_table(matches[[paste0(s, "__full")]]$m, "sum.all") %>% mutate(sample = s, spec = "before")))
## Readable legend labels (the figure is used in the thesis appendix)
SPEC_NAMES_08 <- c(before = "Before matching", full = "Full matching (main)",
                   full_cs = "Full matching, common support", nearest = "Nearest neighbour 3:1",
                   genetic = "Genetic 3:1")
love <- bind_rows(before, balance_after) %>%
  mutate(spec = factor(SPEC_NAMES_08[as.character(spec)], SPEC_NAMES_08),
         sample = recode(sample, full = "Full sample", precovid = "Pre-COVID"))
fig_love <- ggplot(love, aes(x = abs(std_mean_diff), y = reorder(covariate, abs(std_mean_diff)), shape = spec, colour = spec)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = SMD_BALANCED, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = SMD_SERIOUS, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(size = 2) + facet_wrap(~ sample) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c("grey50", "#2a78d6", "#1baf7a", "#eb6834", "#4a3aa7"),
                                        SPEC_NAMES_08)) +
  labs(x = "Absolute standardised mean difference", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
       title = "Covariate balance before and after matching",
       subtitle = "Dashed: 0.10 (balanced). Dotted: 0.25 (serious imbalance).") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2), shape = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "top", legend.text = element_text(size = 11))
ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, "match_balance_love_plot.png"), fig_love, width = 11, height = 6.5, dpi = 200, bg = "white")

## (b) Covariate densities, AD vs non-AD, before and after the main matching (A&M Figures 2 and 4)
density_plot <- function(s) {
  md <- matches[[paste0(s, "__full")]]$md
  bind_rows(SAMPLES[[s]] %>% mutate(weights = 1, stage = "Before matching"),
            md %>% mutate(stage = "After full matching")) %>%
    select(adp_flag, weights, stage, all_of(names(COVARIATES))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(names(COVARIATES)), names_to = "var") %>%
    mutate(covariate = COVARIATES[var], group = if_else(adp_flag == 1, "AD", "Non-AD"),
           stage = factor(stage, c("Before matching", "After full matching"))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(value, weight = weights, colour = group, linetype = stage)) +
    geom_density(linewidth = 0.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ covariate, ncol = 4, scales = "free", labeller = label_wrap_gen(30)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(AD = "#eb6834", "Non-AD" = "#2a78d6")) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Before matching" = "dashed", "After full matching" = "solid")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
         title = paste("Covariate densities, AD vs non-AD,", s, "sample"),
         subtitle = "Dashed: before matching. Solid: after full matching (weighted). AD lines coincide: ADs keep weight 1 (ATT).") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 8) + theme(legend.position = "top")
}
for (s in names(SAMPLES))
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0("match_densities_", s, ".png")), density_plot(s),
         width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```
