## 8.5 Balance after matching with t-tests

For every sample and matching method, the matched non-AD mean of each covariate is compared with the
AD mean, in the same layout as Table 5 (before matching). The difference and its standard error come
from a regression of the covariate on the AD indicator, weighted by the matching weights, with
standard errors clustered by matched set (HC1) and a $t$ distribution with (number of matched sets
$-$ 1) degrees of freedom, as in the ATT-DiD. The chunk checks that the means
reproduce MatchIt's balance table (8.2) exactly.

```{r s08-balance-ttest}
base_t <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_baseline_nosplit.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
bal_t  <- read_csv(file.path(TABLE_DIR, "match_balance_after.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
COV_T  <- unique(bal_t$var)
rows_t <- list()
for (s in c("full", "precovid")) for (sp in c("full", "full_cs", "nearest", "genetic")) {
  m <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, sprintf("matched_%s_%s.csv", s, sp)), show_col_types = FALSE)
  d <- merge(as.data.frame(m[, c("dist_id", "adp_flag", "weights", "subclass")]),
             as.data.frame(base_t[, c("dist_id", COV_T)]), by = "dist_id")
  d <- d[d$weights > 0, ]                     # districts outside the matched sample carry weight 0
  G <- length(unique(d$subclass))             # number of matched sets = clusters
  for (v in COV_T) {
    fit <- lm(as.formula(paste(v, "~ adp_flag")), data = d, weights = weights)
    se  <- sqrt(sandwich::vcovCL(fit, cluster = ~ subclass, type = "HC1")["adp_flag", "adp_flag"])
    b   <- coef(fit)[["adp_flag"]]; tt <- b / se
    w0  <- d$adp_flag == 0
    ref <- bal_t[bal_t$sample == s & bal_t$spec == sp & bal_t$var == v, ]
    rows_t[[length(rows_t) + 1]] <- data.frame(sample = s, spec = sp, var = v, covariate = ref$covariate,
      mean_ad = mean(d[[v]][!w0]), mean_non_ad = weighted.mean(d[[v]][w0], d$weights[w0]),
      smd = ref$std_mean_diff, diff = b, t_stat = tt, p_value = 2 * pt(-abs(tt), df = G - 1), clusters = G,
      check_ad = ref$mean_ad, check_non_ad = ref$mean_non_ad)
  }
}
balance_ttest <- do.call(rbind, rows_t)
## Check: the means reproduce MatchIt's balance table, and the regression slope is the difference in means
stopifnot(max(abs(balance_ttest$mean_ad - balance_ttest$check_ad)) < 1e-6,
          max(abs(balance_ttest$mean_non_ad - balance_ttest$check_non_ad)) < 1e-6,
          max(abs(balance_ttest$diff - (balance_ttest$mean_ad - balance_ttest$mean_non_ad))) < 1e-6)
balance_ttest <- balance_ttest[, setdiff(names(balance_ttest), c("check_ad", "check_non_ad"))]
## Number of covariates significant at 5% after matching, by sample and method
print(aggregate(p_value ~ sample + spec, balance_ttest, function(p) sum(p < 0.05)))
write_csv(balance_ttest, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "match_balance_after_ttest.csv"))

## Comparison of the matching methods (thesis Section 6.3): balance summary from 8.2 plus the
## number of covariates still significantly different at 5% after matching
method_comparison <- read_csv(file.path(TABLE_DIR, "match_summary.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(aggregate(p_value ~ sample + spec, balance_ttest, function(p) sum(p < 0.05)) %>%
              rename(significant_5pct = p_value), by = c("sample", "spec"))
stopifnot(nrow(method_comparison) == 8, !anyNA(method_comparison$significant_5pct))
print(method_comparison, width = Inf)
write_csv(method_comparison, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "match_method_comparison.csv"))
```


# Stage 09: ATT-DiD

The estimator is A&M's Eq. 4: the weighted mean NFHS-4 to NFHS-5 change in ADs minus the weighted
mean change in matched non-ADs, with the Stage 08 matching weights. It is computed directly and as
the AD x post coefficient of a weighted stacked regression, which gives the standard error.

**Specification:**

| | Choice |
|---|---|
| Main estimate | Unadjusted: the A&M replication |
| Adjusted column | Adds `covariate x post` for each covariate with abs(SMD) > 0.10 after matching, in that sample and specification |
| Standard errors | Cluster-robust, clustered by matching subclass |
| Multiple testing | Benjamini-Hochberg, health and empowerment as separate families, per sample and specification |
| Robustness | Common support, nearest neighbour, genetic; weight trimming; leave one state out; water caps 90 and 150; permutation inference |

## 9.1 Check the inputs

Before estimating anything: every matched district must have one NFHS-4 and one NFHS-5 row in the
outcome panels, the same AD flag everywhere, baseline covariates for the adjustment, and a subclass
for clustering. Then, for each specification and outcome, count the districts that drop out because
the outcome is missing in a round, and the share of control weight they carry.

```{r s09-setup}
stopifnot(exists("HEALTH_OUTCOMES"), exists("COVARIATES"))   # defined in Stages 07 and 08
missing_pkgs <- c("sandwich", "lmtest")[!sapply(c("sandwich", "lmtest"), requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_pkgs)) stop("Install first: install.packages(c(\"", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = "\", \""), "\"))")

## Empowerment estimates: education only for women 15-24 (as in Stage 07, Table 6)
EMP_ESTIMATES <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    population = c("married_15_49", "women_15_24"),
    var = c("decision_index", "barrier_index", "educ_years", "water_time_min", "water_within30")) %>%
  filter(!(var == "educ_years" & population == "married_15_49"))

SAMPLES_09 <- c("full", "precovid")
MATCH_SPECS <- c("full", "full_cs", "nearest", "genetic")

matched <- list()
for (s in SAMPLES_09) for (sp in MATCH_SPECS)
  matched[[paste(s, sp, sep = "__")]] <-
    read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, paste0("matched_", s, "_", sp, ".csv")), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(subclass = as.character(subclass))

panel_h <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_panel_nosplit.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
## Main index (PCA weights from NFHS-4, Stage 6.4b) in the decision_index / barrier_index columns,
## so every Stage 09 result, figure and robustness check uses the same index as the thesis.
panel_e_pooled_raw <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_empowerment_nosplit.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
alt_09 <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_empowerment_alt_indices.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(dist_id, survey_round, population, decision_index = decision_index_n4, barrier_index = barrier_index_n4)
panel_e <- panel_e_pooled_raw %>% select(-decision_index, -barrier_index) %>%
  left_join(alt_09, by = c("dist_id", "survey_round", "population"))
## Check: same rows, and each index is missing exactly where the pooled index is missing
stopifnot(nrow(panel_e) == nrow(panel_e_pooled_raw),
          identical(is.na(panel_e$decision_index), is.na(panel_e_pooled_raw$decision_index)),
          identical(is.na(panel_e$barrier_index),  is.na(panel_e_pooled_raw$barrier_index)))
baseline_09 <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_baseline_nosplit.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(dist_id, all_of(names(COVARIATES)))
cat("Health outcomes:", nrow(HEALTH_OUTCOMES), " Empowerment estimates:", nrow(EMP_ESTIMATES), "\n")
```

```{r s09-inputs}
## (a) Panels: exactly one NFHS-4 and one NFHS-5 row per district (and population), one AD flag
round_check <- function(p, keys) p %>% group_by(across(all_of(keys))) %>%
  summarise(n4 = sum(survey_round == "nfhs4"), n5 = sum(survey_round == "nfhs5"),
            flags = n_distinct(adp_flag), .groups = "drop")
h_rounds <- round_check(panel_h, "dist_id")
e_rounds <- round_check(panel_e, c("dist_id", "population"))
stopifnot(all(h_rounds$n4 == 1 & h_rounds$n5 == 1 & h_rounds$flags == 1),
          all(e_rounds$n4 == 1 & e_rounds$n5 == 1 & e_rounds$flags == 1))
cat("Health panel:", nrow(h_rounds), "districts. Empowerment panel:", n_distinct(e_rounds$dist_id),
    "districts x", n_distinct(e_rounds$population), "populations\n")

## (b) Matched samples: keys, weights, subclasses, and links to the panels and covariates
flag_h <- panel_h %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs4") %>% select(dist_id, flag_panel = adp_flag)
match_checks <- bind_rows(lapply(names(matched), function(k) {
  m <- matched[[k]]
  sub <- m %>% group_by(subclass) %>% summarise(n_ad = sum(adp_flag), n_non_ad = sum(adp_flag == 0), .groups = "drop")
  cov_ok <- complete.cases(baseline_09[match(m$dist_id, baseline_09$dist_id), names(COVARIATES)])
  tibble(sample = sub("__.*", "", k), spec = sub(".*__", "", k),
         ad = sum(m$adp_flag == 1), non_ad = sum(m$adp_flag == 0),
         duplicate_ids = sum(duplicated(m$dist_id)),
         ad_weight_not_1 = sum(abs(m$weights[m$adp_flag == 1] - 1) > 1e-8),
         nonpositive_weights = sum(m$weights <= 0),
         missing_subclass = sum(is.na(m$subclass)),
         subclasses = nrow(sub),
         subclass_missing_a_group = sum(sub$n_ad == 0 | sub$n_non_ad == 0),
         max_ad_per_subclass = max(sub$n_ad), max_non_ad_per_subclass = max(sub$n_non_ad),
         not_in_health_panel = sum(!m$dist_id %in% panel_h$dist_id),
         not_in_emp_panel = sum(!m$dist_id %in% panel_e$dist_id),
         ad_flag_mismatch = sum(m$adp_flag != flag_h$flag_panel[match(m$dist_id, flag_h$dist_id)], na.rm = TRUE),
         missing_covariates = sum(!cov_ok))
}))
print(match_checks, width = Inf)
stopifnot(all(match_checks$duplicate_ids == 0), all(match_checks$ad_weight_not_1 == 0),
          all(match_checks$nonpositive_weights == 0), all(match_checks$missing_subclass == 0),
          all(match_checks$subclass_missing_a_group == 0), all(match_checks$not_in_health_panel == 0),
          all(match_checks$not_in_emp_panel == 0), all(match_checks$ad_flag_mismatch == 0),
          all(match_checks$missing_covariates == 0))

## (c) Coverage: districts lost to a missing outcome in either round, by specification
coverage_one <- function(m, pnl, var) {
  wide <- pnl %>% select(dist_id, survey_round, y = all_of(var)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey_round, values_from = y)
  d <- m %>% left_join(wide, by = "dist_id") %>% mutate(ok = !is.na(nfhs4) & !is.na(nfhs5))
  tibble(ad_used = sum(d$ok & d$adp_flag == 1), ad_lost = sum(!d$ok & d$adp_flag == 1),
         non_ad_used = sum(d$ok & d$adp_flag == 0), non_ad_lost = sum(!d$ok & d$adp_flag == 0),
         control_weight_lost_pct = 100 * sum(d$weights[!d$ok & d$adp_flag == 0]) / sum(d$weights[d$adp_flag == 0]))
}
coverage <- bind_rows(lapply(names(matched), function(k) {
  m <- matched[[k]]
  bind_rows(
    bind_rows(lapply(HEALTH_OUTCOMES$var, function(v)
      coverage_one(m, panel_h, v) %>% mutate(family = "health", population = "children/mothers", var = v))),
    bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(EMP_ESTIMATES)), function(i)
      coverage_one(m, filter(panel_e, population == EMP_ESTIMATES$population[i]), EMP_ESTIMATES$var[i]) %>%
        mutate(family = "empowerment", population = EMP_ESTIMATES$population[i], var = EMP_ESTIMATES$var[i])))
  ) %>% mutate(sample = sub("__.*", "", k), spec = sub(".*__", "", k))
})) %>% select(sample, spec, family, population, var, everything())

cat("\nOutcomes that lose any district, main specification (full matching):\n")
print(coverage %>% filter(spec == "full", ad_lost + non_ad_lost > 0) %>%
        mutate(control_weight_lost_pct = round(control_weight_lost_pct, 2)), n = Inf, width = Inf)
cat("\nAll specifications: outcome-sample-spec rows losing any AD:", sum(coverage$ad_lost > 0),
    " largest control weight lost (%):", round(max(coverage$control_weight_lost_pct), 2), "\n")

write_csv(match_checks, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_input_match_checks.csv"))
write_csv(coverage,     file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_input_coverage.csv"))
```


## 9.2 The estimator

One function estimates every ATT. For one matched sample and
one outcome it:

1. keeps districts with the outcome in both rounds and computes each district's change,
   NFHS-5 minus NFHS-4;
2. computes the ATT directly: mean change in ADs minus the weighted mean change in non-ADs
   (A&M Eq. 4; ADs have weight 1 under the ATT);
3. refits it as the AD x post coefficient of a weighted regression on the stacked rounds,
   `y ~ AD * post`, which gives the same number and a standard error;
4. optionally adds `covariate * post` for the covariates passed in `adjust`;
5. clusters the standard error by matching subclass, with p-values from a t distribution
   with (number of subclasses - 1) degrees of freedom, the usual small-cluster correction.

If the direct and regression estimates differ (unadjusted only), it stops: that would mean a bug.

```{r s09-estimator}
att_did <- function(m, pnl, var, adjust = character(0), weight_col = "weights", min_n = 5,
                    cluster_var = "subclass") {
  wide <- pnl %>% select(dist_id, survey_round, y = all_of(var)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey_round, values_from = y)
  d <- m %>% select(dist_id, adp_flag, subclass, w = all_of(weight_col)) %>%
    inner_join(wide, by = "dist_id") %>%
    filter(!is.na(nfhs4), !is.na(nfhs5), w > 0) %>%
    mutate(dy = nfhs5 - nfhs4)
  if (length(adjust)) d <- d %>% left_join(select(baseline_09, dist_id, all_of(adjust)), by = "dist_id")

  res <- tibble(outcome = var, n_ad = sum(d$adp_flag == 1), n_non_ad = sum(d$adp_flag == 0),
                adjusted = length(adjust) > 0, adjust_vars = paste(adjust, collapse = ", "),
                att_direct = NA_real_, att = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, t_stat = NA_real_,
                p_value = NA_real_, clusters = n_distinct(d[[cluster_var]]),
                subclasses_without_controls = sum(tapply(d$adp_flag == 0, d$subclass, sum) == 0),
                mean_change_ad = NA_real_, mean_change_non_ad = NA_real_)
  if (res$n_ad < min_n || res$n_non_ad < min_n) return(res)

  ## (2) Direct double difference
  ad <- d$adp_flag == 1
  res$mean_change_ad     <- weighted.mean(d$dy[ad],  d$w[ad])
  res$mean_change_non_ad <- weighted.mean(d$dy[!ad], d$w[!ad])
  res$att_direct <- res$mean_change_ad - res$mean_change_non_ad

  ## (3)-(4) Stacked weighted regression; AD x post is the ATT
  long <- d %>% tidyr::pivot_longer(c(nfhs4, nfhs5), names_to = "survey_round", values_to = "y") %>%
    mutate(post = as.integer(survey_round == "nfhs5"))
  rhs <- c("adp_flag * post", if (length(adjust)) paste0(adjust, " * post"))
  fit <- lm(reformulate(rhs, response = "y"), data = long, weights = w)

  ## (5) Cluster-robust SE by subclass; t with G - 1 degrees of freedom
  vc <- sandwich::vcovCL(fit, cluster = long[[cluster_var]], type = "HC1")
  res$att    <- unname(coef(fit)["adp_flag:post"])
  res$se     <- sqrt(vc["adp_flag:post", "adp_flag:post"])
  res$t_stat <- res$att / res$se
  res$p_value <- 2 * pt(-abs(res$t_stat), df = res$clusters - 1)

  if (!length(adjust) && abs(res$att - res$att_direct) > 1e-6)
    stop("Direct and regression ATT differ for ", var, ": ", res$att_direct, " vs ", res$att)
  res
}

SMD_BALANCED <- 0.10   # as in Stage 08
## Covariates for the adjusted column: abs(SMD) > 0.10 after matching, per sample and spec,
## read from the Stage 08 balance table.
balance_09 <- read_csv(file.path(TABLE_DIR, "match_balance_after.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
adjust_vars <- function(sample, spec) {
  balance_09 %>% filter(sample == !!sample, spec == !!spec, abs(std_mean_diff) > SMD_BALANCED) %>% pull(var)
}
```

### Check the estimator before using it

(a) A toy example worked by hand. (b) Direct and regression estimates agree for every outcome and
every matched sample. (c) The covariates the adjusted column will use, fixed before any results.

```{r s09-estimator-checks}
## (a) Toy data: ADs change by 2 and 4 (mean 3); non-ADs change by 1, 2, 3 with weights 1, 1, 2,
##     so their weighted mean change is (1 + 2 + 6) / 4 = 2.25. ATT = 3 - 2.25 = 0.75.
toy_m <- tibble(dist_id = 1:5, adp_flag = c(1, 1, 0, 0, 0), subclass = c("a", "b", "a", "b", "b"),
                weights = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 2))
toy_p <- tibble(dist_id = rep(1:5, 2), survey_round = rep(c("nfhs4", "nfhs5"), each = 5),
                y = c(10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 12, 14, 11, 12, 13))
toy <- att_did(toy_m, toy_p, "y", min_n = 1)
cat("Toy ATT:", toy$att, "(expected 0.75)\n")
stopifnot(abs(toy$att - 0.75) < 1e-12, abs(toy$att_direct - 0.75) < 1e-12)

## (b) Agreement of the two forms, all outcomes x all matched samples (att_did stops on a mismatch)
agree <- bind_rows(lapply(names(matched), function(k) {
  m <- matched[[k]]
  bind_rows(
    bind_rows(lapply(HEALTH_OUTCOMES$var, function(v) att_did(m, panel_h, v))),
    bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(EMP_ESTIMATES)), function(i)
      att_did(m, filter(panel_e, population == EMP_ESTIMATES$population[i]), EMP_ESTIMATES$var[i])))
  ) %>% mutate(sample = sub("__.*", "", k), spec = sub(".*__", "", k))
}))
cat("Estimates checked:", nrow(agree), "| largest |direct - regression| gap:",
    signif(max(abs(agree$att - agree$att_direct)), 3), "\n")
print(agree %>% group_by(sample, spec) %>%
        summarise(estimates = n(), clusters_min = min(clusters), clusters_max = max(clusters),
                  subclasses_without_controls = max(subclasses_without_controls), .groups = "drop"))

## (c) Adjusted column: covariates per sample (main specification, full matching)
for (s in SAMPLES_09) cat("Adjust,", s, "sample:", paste(adjust_vars(s, "full"), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```


## 9.3 Main results: health outcomes (A&M Tables 5 and 8)

Full matching, all districts kept, for both samples. Each estimate is reported unadjusted
(the A&M replication) and adjusted. Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values are computed within
each sample and version over the 13 health outcomes, from unrounded p-values.

```{r s09-health-main}
run_family <- function(sample, spec, version = c("unadjusted", "adjusted")) {
  version <- match.arg(version)
  adj <- if (version == "adjusted") adjust_vars(sample, spec) else character(0)
  m <- matched[[paste(sample, spec, sep = "__")]]
  bind_rows(lapply(HEALTH_OUTCOMES$var, function(v) att_did(m, panel_h, v, adjust = adj))) %>%
    mutate(sample = sample, spec = spec, version = version,
           p_bh = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))
}
health_main <- bind_rows(lapply(SAMPLES_09, function(s) bind_rows(
  run_family(s, "full", "unadjusted"), run_family(s, "full", "adjusted")))) %>%
  left_join(HEALTH_OUTCOMES %>% select(no, outcome = var, label), by = "outcome")

## A&M layout: one row per indicator, unadjusted and adjusted side by side
health_table <- health_main %>%
  select(sample, no, label, version, att, se, t_stat, p_value, p_bh, n_ad, n_non_ad) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = version, values_from = c(att, se, t_stat, p_value, p_bh)) %>%
  select(sample, no, label, n_ad, n_non_ad,
         att_unadjusted, se_unadjusted, t_stat_unadjusted, p_value_unadjusted, p_bh_unadjusted,
         att_adjusted, se_adjusted, p_value_adjusted, p_bh_adjusted)

for (s in SAMPLES_09) {
  cat("\n==", if (s == "full") "Full sample (A&M Table 5)" else "Pre-COVID sample (A&M Table 8)", "==\n")
  print(health_table %>% filter(sample == s) %>% select(-sample) %>%
          mutate(across(c(starts_with("att"), starts_with("se"), starts_with("t_stat")), ~ round(.x, 2)),
                 across(starts_with("p_"), ~ round(.x, 3))), n = Inf, width = Inf)
}

## Sign changes or a change in significance at 5% between the two versions
flips <- health_table %>%
  filter(sign(att_unadjusted) != sign(att_adjusted) |
         (p_value_unadjusted < 0.05) != (p_value_adjusted < 0.05)) %>%
  select(sample, no, label, att_unadjusted, p_value_unadjusted, att_adjusted, p_value_adjusted)
cat("\nIndicators where adjustment changes the sign or 5% significance:", nrow(flips), "\n")
if (nrow(flips)) print(flips %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), width = Inf)

write_csv(health_main,  file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_health_main_long.csv"))
write_csv(health_table, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_health_main.csv"))
```


## 9.4 Main results: women's empowerment (the extension)

Same estimator, matched samples and versions as 9.3. The 9 empowerment estimates (4 outcomes for
married women 15-49, 5 for women 15-24) form one Benjamini-Hochberg family per sample and version
Units: the two indices in SD units (higher = more say / more barriers), education in years,
water time in round-trip minutes (capped at 120), water within 30 minutes as a share (0-1).
The last column is the median number of women behind each district mean (Stage 06 cell sizes):
thin cells mean noisy district means. The two indices are the main versions, with PCA weights estimated on NFHS-4
(Stage 6.4b); Stage 10 compares them with the pooled-PCA and alternative indices.

```{r s09-emp-main}
EMP_LABELS <- c(decision_index = "Decision-making index (SD)", barrier_index = "Barrier index (SD)",
                educ_years = "Education (years)", water_time_min = "Water time (minutes)",
                water_within30 = "Water within 30 min (share)")

run_emp_family <- function(sample, spec, version = c("unadjusted", "adjusted")) {
  version <- match.arg(version)
  adj <- if (version == "adjusted") adjust_vars(sample, spec) else character(0)
  m <- matched[[paste(sample, spec, sep = "__")]]
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(EMP_ESTIMATES)), function(i) {
    pop <- EMP_ESTIMATES$population[i]; v <- EMP_ESTIMATES$var[i]
    pnl <- filter(panel_e, population == pop)
    cells <- pnl %>% filter(dist_id %in% m$dist_id) %>% pull(paste0("n_", v))
    att_did(m, pnl, v, adjust = adj) %>%
      mutate(population = pop, median_women = median(cells, na.rm = TRUE))
  })) %>%
    mutate(sample = sample, spec = spec, version = version,
           p_bh = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))
}
emp_main <- bind_rows(lapply(SAMPLES_09, function(s) bind_rows(
  run_emp_family(s, "full", "unadjusted"), run_emp_family(s, "full", "adjusted")))) %>%
  mutate(label = EMP_LABELS[outcome])

emp_table <- emp_main %>%
  select(sample, population, label, version, att, se, p_value, p_bh, n_ad, n_non_ad, median_women,
         mean_change_ad, mean_change_non_ad) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = version,
                     values_from = c(att, se, p_value, p_bh, mean_change_ad, mean_change_non_ad)) %>%
  select(sample, population, label, n_ad, n_non_ad, median_women,
         mean_change_ad = mean_change_ad_unadjusted, mean_change_non_ad = mean_change_non_ad_unadjusted,
         att_unadjusted, se_unadjusted, p_value_unadjusted, p_bh_unadjusted,
         att_adjusted, se_adjusted, p_value_adjusted, p_bh_adjusted)

for (s in SAMPLES_09) {
  cat("\n==", if (s == "full") "Full sample" else "Pre-COVID sample", "==\n")
  print(emp_table %>% filter(sample == s) %>% select(-sample) %>%
          mutate(across(c(starts_with("att"), starts_with("se"), starts_with("mean_change")), ~ round(.x, 3)),
                 across(starts_with("p_"), ~ round(.x, 3))), n = Inf, width = Inf)
}

flips_emp <- emp_table %>%
  filter(sign(att_unadjusted) != sign(att_adjusted) |
         (p_value_unadjusted < 0.05) != (p_value_adjusted < 0.05)) %>%
  select(sample, population, label, att_unadjusted, p_value_unadjusted, att_adjusted, p_value_adjusted)
cat("\nEstimates where adjustment changes the sign or 5% significance:", nrow(flips_emp), "\n")
if (nrow(flips_emp)) print(flips_emp %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), width = Inf)

write_csv(emp_main,  file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_empowerment_main_long.csv"))
write_csv(emp_table, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_empowerment_main.csv"))
```

## 9.4b Robustness: standard errors clustered by district

The main standard errors are clustered by matched set. As a check, the main specification
(full matching, unadjusted) is re-estimated with standard errors clustered by district, with a
t distribution on (number of districts - 1) degrees of freedom. The ATTs are identical; only the
standard errors and p-values change. Benjamini-Hochberg within the nine estimates of each sample.

```{r s09-cluster-district}
emp_cluster_dist <- bind_rows(lapply(SAMPLES_09, function(s) {
  m <- matched[[paste(s, "full", sep = "__")]]
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(EMP_ESTIMATES)), function(i) {
    pop <- EMP_ESTIMATES$population[i]; v <- EMP_ESTIMATES$var[i]
    att_did(m, filter(panel_e, population == pop), v, cluster_var = "dist_id") %>% mutate(population = pop)
  })) %>% mutate(sample = s, p_bh = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))
})) %>% mutate(label = EMP_LABELS[outcome])

## Check: the ATTs equal the main results; only the standard errors differ
chk_cd <- emp_cluster_dist %>%
  inner_join(emp_main %>% filter(version == "unadjusted") %>%
               select(sample, population, outcome, att_main = att, se_main = se, p_main = p_value),
             by = c("sample", "population", "outcome"))
stopifnot(nrow(chk_cd) == nrow(emp_cluster_dist), max(abs(chk_cd$att - chk_cd$att_main)) < 1e-8)
print(chk_cd %>% select(sample, population, label, att, se_main, p_main, se_district = se,
                        p_district = p_value, p_bh_district = p_bh, clusters) %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), n = Inf, width = Inf)
write_csv(emp_cluster_dist, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_cluster_district.csv"))
```


## 9.5 Helpers for the robustness checks

`estimate_all()` runs every health and empowerment estimate on one matched sample, with BH within
each family. `subclass_weights()` rebuilds the full-matching ATT weights from subclass
membership: each AD weight 1, each non-AD (ADs in its subclass) / (non-ADs in its subclass),
rescaled so control weights sum to the number of controls (as MatchIt does). It is needed when
districts are removed (leave one state out) or labels are shuffled (permutation), and it is
checked against the Stage 08 weights first.

```{r s09-helpers}
estimate_all <- function(m, adj = character(0)) {
  h <- bind_rows(lapply(HEALTH_OUTCOMES$var, function(v) att_did(m, panel_h, v, adjust = adj))) %>%
    mutate(family = "health", population = "children/mothers", p_bh = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))
  e <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(EMP_ESTIMATES)), function(i)
      att_did(m, filter(panel_e, population == EMP_ESTIMATES$population[i]), EMP_ESTIMATES$var[i],
              adjust = adj) %>% mutate(population = EMP_ESTIMATES$population[i]))) %>%
    mutate(family = "empowerment", p_bh = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))
  bind_rows(h, e)
}
## Index outcomes only (decision-making and barrier indices, both populations), for Stage 10,
## where only these two outcomes change. Same estimator and order as estimate_all(); no BH
## column, because Stage 10 robustness reports raw p-values only.
INDEX_VARS <- c("decision_index", "barrier_index")
estimate_index <- function(m, adj = character(0)) {
  ix <- which(EMP_ESTIMATES$var %in% INDEX_VARS)
  bind_rows(lapply(ix, function(i)
      att_did(m, filter(panel_e, population == EMP_ESTIMATES$population[i]), EMP_ESTIMATES$var[i],
              adjust = adj) %>% mutate(population = EMP_ESTIMATES$population[i]))) %>%
    mutate(family = "empowerment")
}
label_of <- function(outcome, family)
  ifelse(family == "health", HEALTH_OUTCOMES$label[match(outcome, HEALTH_OUTCOMES$var)], EMP_LABELS[outcome])
no_of <- function(outcome) HEALTH_OUTCOMES$no[match(outcome, HEALTH_OUTCOMES$var)]
## Panel title and order for figures: health in A&M order (with indicator number), then empowerment
panel_of <- function(family, population, outcome) {
  title <- ifelse(family == "health", paste(no_of(outcome), label_of(outcome, family)),
                  paste0(label_of(outcome, family), ", ", sub("_(\\d+)_(\\d+)$", " \\1-\\2", population)))
  ord <- ifelse(family == "health", match(outcome, HEALTH_OUTCOMES$var),
                100 + match(paste(population, outcome), paste(EMP_ESTIMATES$population, EMP_ESTIMATES$var)))
  factor(title, levels = unique(title[order(ord)]))
}

subclass_weights <- function(adp, subclass) {
  n_t <- ave(adp, subclass, FUN = sum); n_c <- ave(1 - adp, subclass, FUN = sum)
  w <- ifelse(adp == 1, 1, n_t / n_c)
  ctrl <- adp == 0
  w[ctrl] <- w[ctrl] * sum(ctrl) / sum(w[ctrl])
  w
}
ess <- function(w) sum(w)^2 / sum(w^2)   # effective sample size of a set of weights

## Check: rebuilt weights equal the Stage 08 weights for every matched sample
w_check <- sapply(matched, function(m) max(abs(subclass_weights(m$adp_flag, m$subclass) - m$weights)))
print(signif(w_check, 3))
stopifnot(all(w_check < 1e-8))
```

## 9.6 Robustness: alternative matching (A&M Tables 9 and 10)

Common support (`full_cs`), nearest neighbour 3:1 and genetic 3:1, unadjusted, for all outcomes in
both samples. Together with 9.3 and 9.4 this gives one long table of every estimate (`att_all`).

```{r s09-robust-matching}
robust_match <- bind_rows(lapply(SAMPLES_09, function(s) bind_rows(lapply(c("full_cs", "nearest", "genetic"),
  function(sp) estimate_all(matched[[paste(s, sp, sep = "__")]]) %>%
    mutate(sample = s, spec = sp, version = "unadjusted")))))

att_all <- bind_rows(
    health_main %>% mutate(family = "health", population = "children/mothers"),
    emp_main %>% mutate(family = "empowerment"),
    robust_match) %>%
  mutate(no = no_of(outcome), label = label_of(outcome, family),
         spec_label = case_when(spec == "full" & version == "unadjusted" ~ "Main (full matching)",
                                spec == "full" & version == "adjusted" ~ "Main, adjusted",
                                spec == "full_cs" ~ "Common support",
                                spec == "nearest" ~ "Nearest neighbour 3:1",
                                spec == "genetic" ~ "Genetic 3:1")) %>%
  select(sample, family, population, outcome, no, label, spec, version, spec_label,
         n_ad, n_non_ad, att, se, t_stat, p_value, p_bh, clusters, mean_change_ad, mean_change_non_ad,
         adjust_vars)

## Compact view: ATT (p-value) by specification
compact <- function(d) d %>%
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", att, p_value)) %>%
  select(sample, family, population, label, spec_label, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = spec_label, values_from = cell)
for (s in SAMPLES_09) {
  cat("\n==", s, "sample: ATT (p-value) ==\n")
  print(compact(filter(att_all, sample == s)) %>% select(-sample), n = Inf, width = Inf)
}
write_csv(att_all, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_all_specifications.csv"))
```

## 9.8 Robustness: trimming the largest control weights

Under full matching a few non-ADs carry much of the control weight (Stage 08: the top 10 carry
36% / 53%). Here control weights above their 99th (95th) percentile are capped at that percentile
and everything is re-estimated (main specification, unadjusted). The effective sample size (ESS)
of the controls shows how much the cap spreads the weight.

```{r s09-trim}
trim_weights <- function(m, pct) {
  ctrl <- m$adp_flag == 0
  cap <- unname(quantile(m$weights[ctrl], 1 - pct / 100))
  m$weights[ctrl] <- pmin(m$weights[ctrl], cap)
  m
}
trim_results <- list(); trim_info <- list()
for (s in SAMPLES_09) for (pct in c(1, 5)) {
  m0 <- matched[[paste(s, "full", sep = "__")]]; m1 <- trim_weights(m0, pct)
  ctrl <- m0$adp_flag == 0
  trim_info[[length(trim_info) + 1]] <- tibble(sample = s, trim_pct = pct,
    cap = max(m1$weights[ctrl]), controls_capped = sum(m0$weights[ctrl] > max(m1$weights[ctrl])),
    top10_weight_share = sum(sort(m0$weights[ctrl], decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]) / sum(m0$weights[ctrl]),
    ess_before = ess(m0$weights[ctrl]), ess_after = ess(m1$weights[ctrl]))
  trim_results[[length(trim_results) + 1]] <- estimate_all(m1) %>% mutate(sample = s, trim_pct = pct)
}
trim_info <- bind_rows(trim_info); print(trim_info %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))))

trim_table <- bind_rows(trim_results) %>%
  mutate(label = label_of(outcome, family)) %>%
  select(sample, family, population, outcome, label, trim_pct, att, se, p_value) %>%
  left_join(att_all %>% filter(spec == "full", version == "unadjusted") %>%
              select(sample, family, population, outcome, att_main = att, p_main = p_value),
            by = c("sample", "family", "population", "outcome")) %>%
  mutate(sign_flip = sign(att) != sign(att_main),
         sig_change = (p_value < 0.05) != (p_main < 0.05),
         pct_change = 100 * (att - att_main) / abs(att_main))
cat("\nEstimates whose sign flips or 5% significance changes under trimming:\n")
print(trim_table %>% filter(sign_flip | sig_change) %>%
        select(sample, population, label, trim_pct, att_main, p_main, att, p_value) %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), n = Inf, width = Inf)
write_csv(trim_info,  file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_trim_info.csv"))
write_csv(trim_table, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_trim.csv"))
```

## 9.9 Robustness: leave one state out (both samples)

Drop every district of one state, keep the remaining matched sets (a subclass that loses all its
ADs or all its non-ADs is dropped), rebuild the weights from the subclasses, and re-estimate
(main specification, unadjusted). If one state drives a result, dropping it moves the estimate
far from the main one. It is run on both samples: in the full sample three states hold 42 of the
102 ADs (Jharkhand 19, Bihar 13, Odisha 10), and Jharkhand is not in the pre-COVID sample.

```{r s09-loso}
loso_one <- function(m, st, est = estimate_all) {
  m2 <- m %>% filter(state_name != st) %>%
    group_by(subclass) %>% filter(any(adp_flag == 1), any(adp_flag == 0)) %>% ungroup()
  m2$weights <- subclass_weights(m2$adp_flag, m2$subclass)
  est(m2) %>% mutate(state_dropped = st, ad_dropped = sum(m$adp_flag[m$state_name == st]))
}
m_pc <- matched[["precovid__full"]]   # also used in Stage 10
## Every state in the sample's main matched data, dropped in turn (states with no AD included:
## dropping them changes the control group)
loso_sample <- function(s, est = estimate_all) {
  m <- matched[[paste(s, "full", sep = "__")]]
  bind_rows(lapply(sort(unique(m$state_name)), function(st) loso_one(m, st, est))) %>%
    mutate(sample = s, .before = 1)
}
## (rebuilt weights already checked against Stage 08 for every matched sample in s09-helpers)
loso <- bind_rows(lapply(SAMPLES_09, loso_sample)) %>%
  mutate(label = label_of(outcome, family)) %>%
  left_join(att_all %>% filter(spec == "full", version == "unadjusted") %>%
              select(sample, family, population, outcome, att_main = att, p_main = p_value),
            by = c("sample", "family", "population", "outcome"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(loso$att_main))

loso_summary <- loso %>% group_by(sample, family, population, outcome, label, att_main, p_main) %>%
  summarise(att_min = min(att, na.rm = TRUE), state_at_min = state_dropped[which.min(att)],
            att_max = max(att, na.rm = TRUE), state_at_max = state_dropped[which.max(att)],
            states_flipping_sign = sum(sign(att) != sign(att_main), na.rm = TRUE),
            states_changing_sig5 = sum((p_value < 0.05) != (p_main < 0.05), na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
print(loso %>% distinct(sample, state_dropped, ad_dropped) %>% arrange(sample, desc(ad_dropped)), n = Inf)
print(loso_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), n = Inf, width = Inf)

## Figure: the four estimates of most interest, one point per state dropped
KEY <- tibble::tribble(~family, ~population, ~outcome,
  "health", "children/mothers", "pct_underweight",
  "health", "children/mothers", "pct_breastfed_1hr",
  "empowerment", "married_15_49", "decision_index",
  "empowerment", "women_15_24", "decision_index")
for (s in SAMPLES_09) {
  fig_loso <- loso %>% filter(sample == s) %>% semi_join(KEY, by = c("family", "population", "outcome")) %>%
    mutate(panel = panel_of(family, population, outcome)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = att, y = reorder(state_dropped, ad_dropped))) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
    geom_vline(aes(xintercept = att_main), colour = "#eb6834", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(colour = "#2a78d6", size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
    labs(x = "ATT with the state dropped", y = "State dropped (ordered by ADs dropped)",
         title = paste0("Leave one state out, ", if (s == "full") "full" else "pre-COVID", " sample"),
         subtitle = "Orange line: main estimate with all states. Grey line: zero.") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0("att_loso_", s, ".png")), fig_loso,
         width = 9, height = if (s == "full") 9 else 7, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
}

write_csv(loso,         file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_loso.csv"))
write_csv(loso_summary, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_loso_summary.csv"))
```

## 9.11 Permutation inference

If ADP had no effect, which districts within a matched set are the ADs should not matter. Within
each subclass, the AD labels are shuffled at random (the number of ADs per subclass is kept), the
weights are rebuilt, and the ATT is recomputed; 1,000 times. The permutation p-value is the share
of shuffled ATTs at least as large in absolute value as the real one. It does not rely on
large-sample standard errors, which matters with 28 clusters pre-COVID. Main specification,
unadjusted; the real ATT here is the direct double difference, identical to 9.3 and 9.4.

```{r s09-permutation}
PERM_DRAWS <- 1000
change_matrix <- function(m) {
  one <- function(pnl, v) {
    w <- pnl %>% select(dist_id, survey_round, y = all_of(v)) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey_round, values_from = y)
    w <- w[match(m$dist_id, w$dist_id), ]
    w$nfhs5 - w$nfhs4
  }
  cols <- c(lapply(HEALTH_OUTCOMES$var, function(v) one(panel_h, v)),
            lapply(seq_len(nrow(EMP_ESTIMATES)), function(i)
              one(filter(panel_e, population == EMP_ESTIMATES$population[i]), EMP_ESTIMATES$var[i])))
  D <- do.call(cbind, cols)
  attr(D, "key") <- bind_rows(
    tibble(family = "health", population = "children/mothers", outcome = HEALTH_OUTCOMES$var),
    EMP_ESTIMATES %>% transmute(family = "empowerment", population, outcome = var))
  D
}
att_matrix <- function(adp, w, D) {
  A <- !is.na(D); Dz <- D; Dz[!A] <- 0
  wt <- w * adp; wc <- w * (1 - adp)
  colSums(Dz * wt) / colSums(A * wt) - colSums(Dz * wc) / colSums(A * wc)
}
## Keep only some outcome columns of a change matrix (and the matching rows of its key)
subset_D <- function(D, keep) {
  key <- attr(D, "key"); D2 <- D[, keep, drop = FALSE]; attr(D2, "key") <- key[keep, ]; D2
}
## Permutation test within matched sets: shuffle AD labels inside each subclass, rebuild the
## weights, re-estimate. Each draw uses the RNG only through the shuffles, which depend on the
## matched sets and not on D, so the draws are the same whichever outcomes D holds.
perm_test <- function(m, D) {
  obs <- att_matrix(m$adp_flag, m$weights, D)
  draws <- matrix(replicate(PERM_DRAWS, {
    adp_p <- ave(m$adp_flag, m$subclass, FUN = function(x) x[sample.int(length(x))])
    att_matrix(adp_p, subclass_weights(adp_p, m$subclass), D)
  }), nrow = ncol(D))
  list(obs = obs, draws = draws,
       p_perm = (1 + rowSums(abs(draws) >= abs(obs) - 1e-12)) / (PERM_DRAWS + 1))
}

set.seed(SEED)
perm <- list(); perm_draws <- list()
for (s in SAMPLES_09) {
  m <- matched[[paste(s, "full", sep = "__")]]
  D <- change_matrix(m); key <- attr(D, "key")
  pt <- perm_test(m, D); obs <- pt$obs; draws <- pt$draws
  main <- att_all %>% filter(sample == s, spec == "full", version == "unadjusted")
  main_att <- main$att[match(paste(key$family, key$population, key$outcome),
                             paste(main$family, main$population, main$outcome))]
  stopifnot(max(abs(obs - main_att)) < 1e-8)   # same ATT as 9.3 and 9.4
  perm[[s]] <- key %>% mutate(sample = s, att = obs, p_perm = pt$p_perm,
    p_cluster = main$p_value[match(paste(family, population, outcome),
                                   paste(main$family, main$population, main$outcome))])
  perm_draws[[s]] <- as_tibble(t(draws), .name_repair = ~ paste0("e", seq_along(obs))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "k", values_to = "att_perm") %>%
    mutate(k = as.integer(sub("e", "", k))) %>%
    left_join(key %>% mutate(k = row_number(), att_obs = obs), by = "k") %>% mutate(sample = s)
}
perm <- bind_rows(perm) %>% mutate(label = label_of(outcome, family))
print(perm %>% select(sample, population, label, att, p_cluster, p_perm) %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), n = Inf, width = Inf)

## Figures: distribution of shuffled ATTs with the real ATT marked, one panel per estimate.
## One figure per sample and family (empowerment: thesis appendix; health: replication).
for (s in SAMPLES_09) for (f in c("empowerment", "health")) {
  fig_perm <- perm_draws[[s]] %>% filter(family == f) %>%
    mutate(panel = panel_of(family, population, outcome)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(att_perm)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#2a78d6", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_vline(aes(xintercept = att_obs), colour = "#eb6834", linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free", ncol = if (f == "health") 4 else 3, labeller = label_wrap_gen(32)) +
    labs(x = "ATT with AD labels shuffled within matched sets", y = "Draws",
         title = paste0("Permutation inference, ", f, ", ", s, " sample (", PERM_DRAWS, " draws)"),
         subtitle = "Orange line: the real ATT.") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = if (f == "health") 8 else 10) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0("att_permutation_", f, "_", s, ".png")), fig_perm,
         width = 11, height = if (f == "health") 10 else 7.5, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
}
write_csv(perm, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_permutation.csv"))
```

## 9.12 Summary table and coefficient plots

One row per estimate: the main ATT with its cluster and permutation p-values, the adjusted
version, the three alternative matchings, the 5% trim, and the leave-one-state-out range
(both samples). The coefficient plots show each estimate with its 95% confidence interval under
each specification (t with clusters - 1 df, as in the p-values).

```{r s09-summary}
wide_att <- att_all %>% select(sample, family, population, outcome, spec_label, att, p_value) %>%
  mutate(spec_label = recode(spec_label, "Main (full matching)" = "main", "Main, adjusted" = "adjusted",
                             "Common support" = "common_support", "Nearest neighbour 3:1" = "nearest",
                             "Genetic 3:1" = "genetic")) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = spec_label, values_from = c(att, p_value))
att_summary <- wide_att %>%
  left_join(perm %>% select(sample, family, population, outcome, p_perm),
            by = c("sample", "family", "population", "outcome")) %>%
  left_join(trim_table %>% filter(trim_pct == 5) %>%
              select(sample, family, population, outcome, att_trim5 = att, p_trim5 = p_value),
            by = c("sample", "family", "population", "outcome")) %>%
  left_join(loso_summary %>% transmute(sample, family, population, outcome,
                                       loso_min = att_min, loso_max = att_max),
            by = c("sample", "family", "population", "outcome")) %>%
  mutate(no = no_of(outcome), label = label_of(outcome, family), .after = outcome) %>%
  select(sample, family, population, no, label, att_main, p_value_main, p_perm,
         att_adjusted, p_value_adjusted, att_common_support, p_value_common_support,
         att_nearest, p_value_nearest, att_genetic, p_value_genetic, att_trim5, p_trim5,
         loso_min, loso_max)
write_csv(att_summary, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_summary.csv"))

## Main results table (thesis Section 7.1): empowerment, full matching, both samples.
## Unadjusted and covariate-adjusted ATT, each with its raw and Benjamini-Hochberg p-value,
## and the permutation p-value of the unadjusted ATT.
## 95% confidence interval with the same t(G - 1) critical value as the p-values
att_main_table <- emp_main %>%
  mutate(ci_low  = att - qt(0.975, df = clusters - 1) * se,
         ci_high = att + qt(0.975, df = clusters - 1) * se) %>%
  select(sample, population, outcome, label, version, att, se, ci_low, ci_high, p_value, p_bh, n_ad, n_non_ad) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = version, values_from = c(att, se, ci_low, ci_high, p_value, p_bh)) %>%
  left_join(perm %>% filter(family == "empowerment") %>% select(sample, population, outcome, p_perm),
            by = c("sample", "population", "outcome"))
stopifnot(nrow(att_main_table) == 2 * nrow(EMP_ESTIMATES), !anyNA(att_main_table$p_perm))
write_csv(att_main_table, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_empowerment_main_table.csv"))

## Coefficient plots: one panel per estimate, one row per specification
SPEC_COLOURS <- c("Main (full matching)" = "#2a78d6", "Main, adjusted" = "#eb6834",
                  "Common support" = "#1baf7a", "Nearest neighbour 3:1" = "#eda100",
                  "Genetic 3:1" = "#e87ba4", "Trimmed 5%" = "#008300")
coef_data <- bind_rows(
    att_all,
    trim_table %>% filter(trim_pct == 5) %>%
      left_join(bind_rows(trim_results) %>% filter(trim_pct == 5) %>%
                  select(sample, family, population, outcome, clusters),
                by = c("sample", "family", "population", "outcome")) %>%
      mutate(spec_label = "Trimmed 5%")) %>%
  mutate(crit = qt(0.975, df = clusters - 1), lo = att - crit * se, hi = att + crit * se,

for (s in SAMPLES_09) for (f in c("health", "empowerment")) {

}
```

The main water outcome is the time-only measure, water within 30 minutes round trip. The appendix
uses the full WHO/UNICEF JMP definition of basic service: an improved source **and** collection
within 30 minutes (Stage 06, `water_basic_jmp`, improved sources per FR375). Main specification
(full matching, all ADs), unadjusted and adjusted, both samples and populations. It is reported
next to the time-only measure so the two can be compared directly. No BH adjustment: this is a
single appendix check, not part of the main families.

```{r s09-jmp-appendix}

for (s in SAMPLES_09) for (pop in c("married_15_49", "women_15_24")) for (v in c("water_within30", "water_basic_jmp")) {
  m   <- matched[[paste(s, "full", sep = "__")]]

}
```

## 9.14 Multiple testing: separate vs pooled families

The main results adjust health (13 outcomes) and empowerment (9 estimates) as separate
Benjamini-Hochberg families. The alternative pools all 22 estimates into one family per sample,
specification and version. Both are reported. Pooling makes the adjustment stricter for each
estimate, because there are more tests in the family.

```{r s09-bh-pooled}
bh_compare <- att_all %>%
  group_by(sample, spec, version) %>%
  mutate(p_bh_pooled = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(p_bh_separate = p_bh) %>%
  select(sample, spec_label, family, population, no, label, att, p_value, p_bh_separate, p_bh_pooled)

## Estimates with raw p < 0.10, and how each adjustment treats them
print(bh_compare %>% filter(p_value < 0.10) %>%
        mutate(across(c(att, p_value, p_bh_separate, p_bh_pooled), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
        arrange(sample, spec_label, p_value), n = Inf, width = Inf)
cat("\nEstimates with BH-adjusted p < 0.05: separate families", sum(bh_compare$p_bh_separate < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    "| pooled family", sum(bh_compare$p_bh_pooled < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
write_csv(bh_compare, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_bh_separate_vs_pooled.csv"))
```

# Stage 10: Pre-treatment index weights

Re-estimates the two index outcomes with the indices built in 6.4b, using the Stage 09 estimator
and matched samples unchanged:

- **NFHS-4 PCA** (`_n4`): the main index. It gets the full Stage 09
  treatment: main specification unadjusted and adjusted with BH, the alternative matchings,
  weight trimming, leave one state out (both samples) and permutation inference.
- **Equal-weighted** (`_ew`) and **Anderson** (`_and`): appendix robustness, main specification,
  both samples, unadjusted and adjusted, compared with both PCA versions.

Stage 09 already uses the NFHS-4 PCA index, so 10.1 and 10.2 reproduce its index results (checked)
and add the comparison with the pooled PCA. Only the two indices change; education and water are
the Stage 09 results.
Stage 09 functions read the district panel `panel_e`, so each run below swaps in a panel whose
`decision_index` and `barrier_index` columns hold the chosen version, then restores the original.

```{r s10-setup}
alt_panel <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_empowerment_alt_indices.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
panel_e_pooled <- panel_e_pooled_raw                       # pooled-PCA indices (Stage 06); Stage 09 uses the NFHS-4 index
stopifnot(nrow(alt_panel) == nrow(panel_e_pooled))

## Panel with the chosen index version in the decision_index / barrier_index columns
panel_version <- function(v) {
  if (v == "pooled") return(panel_e_pooled)
  panel_e_pooled %>% select(-decision_index, -barrier_index) %>%
    left_join(alt_panel %>% select(dist_id, survey_round, population,
                                   decision_index = !!paste0("decision_index_", v),
                                   barrier_index  = !!paste0("barrier_index_", v)),
              by = c("dist_id", "survey_round", "population"))
}
## Run any Stage 09 code with panel_e temporarily set to one version
with_panel <- function(v, expr) {
  old <- panel_e; on.exit(panel_e <<- old)
  panel_e <<- panel_version(v)
  force(expr)
}
INDEX_VERSIONS <- c(pooled = "Pooled PCA (Stage 06)", n4 = "NFHS-4 PCA (main)",
                    ew = "Equal-weighted", and = "Anderson (2008)")
IS_INDEX <- function(d) d$family == "empowerment" & d$outcome %in% c("decision_index", "barrier_index")

## Check: the panel for every version pairs both rounds for every district and population
for (v in names(INDEX_VERSIONS)) {
  p <- panel_version(v)
  stopifnot(nrow(p) == nrow(panel_e_pooled), all(count(p, dist_id, population)$n == 2))
}
## Check: the NFHS-4 version is the panel Stage 09 used
chk_n4 <- panel_version("n4") %>% select(dist_id, survey_round, population, d4 = decision_index, b4 = barrier_index) %>%
  inner_join(panel_e %>% select(dist_id, survey_round, population, decision_index, barrier_index),
             by = c("dist_id", "survey_round", "population"))
stopifnot(nrow(chk_n4) == nrow(panel_e), isTRUE(all.equal(chk_n4$d4, chk_n4$decision_index)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(chk_n4$b4, chk_n4$barrier_index)))
```

## 10.1 NFHS-4 PCA: main results

```{r s10-main}
emp_main_n4 <- with_panel("n4", bind_rows(lapply(SAMPLES_09, function(s) bind_rows(
  run_emp_family(s, "full", "unadjusted"), run_emp_family(s, "full", "adjusted"))))) %>%
  mutate(label = EMP_LABELS[outcome])

## Check: identical to the Stage 09 results, which already use the NFHS-4 index
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(emp_main_n4$att, emp_main$att)), isTRUE(all.equal(emp_main_n4$p_value, emp_main$p_value)))

## Side by side with the pooled-PCA index (index outcomes only)
emp_main_pooled <- with_panel("pooled", bind_rows(lapply(SAMPLES_09, function(s) bind_rows(
  run_emp_family(s, "full", "unadjusted"), run_emp_family(s, "full", "adjusted"))))) %>%
  mutate(label = EMP_LABELS[outcome])
main_compare <- bind_rows(
    emp_main_pooled %>% mutate(index_version = "pooled"),
    emp_main_n4 %>% mutate(index_version = "n4")) %>%
  filter(outcome %in% c("decision_index", "barrier_index")) %>%
  select(sample, population, label, version, index_version, att, se, p_value, p_bh,
         mean_change_ad, mean_change_non_ad) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = index_version, values_from = c(att, se, p_value, p_bh, mean_change_ad, mean_change_non_ad))
print(main_compare %>% select(sample, population, label, version, att_pooled, p_value_pooled,
                              att_n4, se_n4, p_value_n4, p_bh_n4) %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), n = Inf, width = Inf)
write_csv(emp_main_n4,  file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_empowerment_main_n4.csv"))
write_csv(main_compare, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_index_pooled_vs_n4.csv"))
```

## 10.2 NFHS-4 PCA: robustness

The Stage 09 checks re-run with the NFHS-4 index: alternative matchings, 1% and 5% weight
trimming, leave one state out (both samples) and permutation inference (1,000 draws, same seed).
Only the two index outcomes are estimated (`estimate_index()`), because nothing else changes in
Stage 10; the permutation draws are the same as with all outcomes (see `perm_test()`).

```{r s10-robust}
robust_n4 <- with_panel("n4", {
  rm_spec <- bind_rows(lapply(SAMPLES_09, function(s) bind_rows(lapply(c("full_cs", "nearest", "genetic"),
    function(sp) estimate_index(matched[[paste(s, sp, sep = "__")]]) %>% mutate(sample = s, check = sp)))))
  rm_trim <- bind_rows(lapply(SAMPLES_09, function(s) bind_rows(lapply(c(1, 5), function(pct)
    estimate_index(trim_weights(matched[[paste(s, "full", sep = "__")]], pct)) %>%
      mutate(sample = s, check = paste0("trim_", pct))))))
  rm_loso <- bind_rows(lapply(SAMPLES_09, loso_sample, est = estimate_index)) %>% mutate(check = "loso")
  ## Permutation: same procedure and seed as 9.11
  set.seed(SEED)
  rm_perm <- bind_rows(lapply(SAMPLES_09, function(s) {
    m <- matched[[paste(s, "full", sep = "__")]]
    D <- change_matrix(m)
    D <- subset_D(D, which(attr(D, "key")$outcome %in% INDEX_VARS))   # index columns only
    pt <- perm_test(m, D)
    attr(D, "key") %>% mutate(sample = s, att = pt$obs, p_perm = pt$p_perm)
  }))
  list(spec = rm_spec, trim = rm_trim, loso = rm_loso, perm = rm_perm)
})

## One row per index estimate: main, permutation, alternative matchings, trimming, LOSO range
idx <- function(d) d %>% filter(IS_INDEX(d))
main_n4 <- idx(emp_main_n4 %>% filter(version == "unadjusted") %>% mutate(family = "empowerment")) %>%
  select(sample, population, outcome, att_main = att, p_main = p_value)
robust_n4_table <- main_n4 %>%
  left_join(idx(robust_n4$perm) %>% select(sample, population, outcome, p_perm),
            by = c("sample", "population", "outcome")) %>%
  left_join(idx(bind_rows(robust_n4$spec, robust_n4$trim)) %>%
              select(sample, population, outcome, check, att, p_value) %>%
              tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = check, values_from = c(att, p_value)),
            by = c("sample", "population", "outcome")) %>%
  left_join(idx(robust_n4$loso) %>%
              left_join(main_n4 %>% select(sample, population, outcome, p_main), by = c("sample", "population", "outcome")) %>%
              group_by(sample, population, outcome) %>%
              summarise(loso_min = min(att, na.rm = TRUE), loso_max = max(att, na.rm = TRUE),
                        loso_states_changing_sig5 = sum((p_value < 0.05) != (p_main < 0.05), na.rm = TRUE),
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("sample", "population", "outcome")) %>%
  mutate(label = EMP_LABELS[outcome], .after = outcome)
print(robust_n4_table %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))), n = Inf, width = Inf)
write_csv(robust_n4_table, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_index_n4_robustness.csv"))
```

## 10.3 Appendix: does the result depend on the weighting?

The two index outcomes under all four weightings, main specification (full matching, all ADs),
unadjusted and adjusted. If the estimates agree, the findings do not depend on PCA weighting.

```{r s10-index-compare}
index_compare <- bind_rows(lapply(names(INDEX_VERSIONS), function(v) with_panel(v, {
  rows <- list()
  for (s in SAMPLES_09) for (pop in c("married_15_49", "women_15_24")) for (o in c("decision_index", "barrier_index")) {
    m   <- matched[[paste(s, "full", sep = "__")]]
    pnl <- filter(panel_e, population == pop)
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- bind_rows(att_did(m, pnl, o), att_did(m, pnl, o, adjust = adjust_vars(s, "full"))) %>%
      mutate(sample = s, population = pop)
  }
  bind_rows(rows) %>% mutate(index_version = v)
}))) %>%
  mutate(version = if_else(adjusted, "adjusted", "unadjusted"),
         index_label = INDEX_VERSIONS[index_version], label = EMP_LABELS[outcome])

print(index_compare %>%
        mutate(cell = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", att, p_value)) %>%
        select(sample, population, label, version, index_label, cell) %>%
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = index_label, values_from = cell) %>%
        arrange(sample, version, label, population), n = Inf, width = Inf)
write_csv(index_compare, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "att_appendix_index_weighting.csv"))
```

# Stage 11: Treatment variable validation

Checks that the treatment indicator is T = 1 for Aspirational Districts and only for them, and
accounts for every one of the 112 official ADs. Uses the files built in
Stages 02, 05 and 08; nothing is recomputed.

1. The official list (NITI Aayog, 112 districts; `data/lookups/adp_official_list.csv`) has no
   duplicates and no West Bengal district.
2. Every official AD is matched to exactly one district code in each NFHS round.
3. **No false positives or negatives:** the NFHS-4 districts with `adp_flag = 1` are exactly the
   codes of the official ADs, and in NFHS-5 a kept district is flagged if and only if it is an
   official AD.
4. **Every official AD accounted for**, with the reason if it is not in the estimation sample.
5. ADs by state: official count against the count in the sample.
6. In every matched sample the treated group is exactly the ADs in that sample, each with weight 1.

```{r s11-treatment}
official <- read_csv(file.path(LOOKUP_DIR, "adp_official_list.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
xwalk    <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "adp_nfhs_crosswalk.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
nmap     <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_nosplit_map.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
base_ns  <- read_csv(file.path(INTER_DIR, "district_baseline_nosplit.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
full_ids <- base_ns %>% filter(if_all(all_of(names(COVARIATES)), ~ !is.na(.x))) %>% pull(dist_id)

## (1) The official list
stopifnot(nrow(official) == 112,
          !anyDuplicated(official[c("state", "district_current_list")]),
          !any(grepl("bengal", tolower(official$state))))

## (2) Each official AD matched once in each round
stopifnot(nrow(xwalk) == 224, all(count(xwalk, state, district, survey_round)$n == 1),
          setequal(paste(official$state, official$district_current_list), paste(xwalk$state, xwalk$district)))
ad4 <- xwalk %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs4")
ad5 <- xwalk %>% filter(survey_round == "nfhs5")

## (3) Flags agree with the official list in both rounds
stopifnot(setequal(unique(ad4$distcode), nmap$distcode[nmap$adp_flag == 1]))
kept <- nmap %>% filter(in_sample)
stopifnot(all((kept$nfhs5_distcode %in% ad5$distcode) == (kept$adp_flag == 1)),
          all(kept$adp_flag == kept$adp_flag_nfhs5))
shared <- ad4 %>% count(distcode) %>% filter(n > 1) %>% pull(distcode)   # NFHS-4 codes holding 2 ADs
cat("Official ADs: 112 | NFHS-4 codes with adp_flag = 1:", n_distinct(ad4$distcode),
    "| codes holding two ADs:", paste(nmap$district_name[nmap$distcode %in% shared], collapse = ", "), "\n")

## (4) Every official AD and where it ends up
ad_status <- official %>%
  select(sno = sno_112_list, state, district = district_current_list, district_2018 = district_2018_ranking) %>%
  left_join(ad4 %>% select(state, district, nfhs4_code = distcode, nfhs4_match = match_type, nfhs4_note = note),
            by = c("state", "district")) %>%
  left_join(ad5 %>% select(state, district, nfhs5_code = distcode), by = c("state", "district")) %>%
  left_join(nmap %>% select(nfhs4_code = distcode, nfhs4_district = district_name, nfhs4_state = state_name,
                            split_parent, mixed_parent, in_sample), by = "nfhs4_code") %>%
  mutate(shares_nfhs4_code = nfhs4_code %in% shared,
         in_full_sample = nfhs4_code %in% full_ids & in_sample,
         in_precovid    = in_full_sample & nfhs4_state %in% PHASE1_STATES_NFHS4,
         status = case_when(
           in_full_sample ~ "In sample",
           in_sample ~ "Dropped: missing matching covariate",
           split_parent & mixed_parent ~ "Dropped: NFHS-4 district later split into AD and non-AD parts",
           split_parent ~ "Dropped: NFHS-4 district later split (all parts are ADs)",
           TRUE ~ "CHECK"))
stopifnot(!any(ad_status$status == "CHECK"), !anyNA(ad_status$nfhs4_code), !anyNA(ad_status$nfhs5_code))
print(count(ad_status, status))
print(ad_status %>% filter(status != "In sample") %>%
        select(state, district, nfhs4_district, shares_nfhs4_code, status) %>% arrange(state), n = Inf, width = Inf)

## Flow from 112 official ADs to the estimation samples (AD rows and NFHS-4 AD codes)
treatment_flow <- tibble(
  step = c("Official list (NITI Aayog)", "Matched to an NFHS-4 district code",
           "Kept: same boundaries in both rounds (Stage 05)", "Full estimation sample (Stage 07/08)",
           "Pre-COVID sample"),
  official_ads = c(nrow(ad_status), sum(!is.na(ad_status$nfhs4_code)), sum(ad_status$in_sample),
                   sum(ad_status$in_full_sample), sum(ad_status$in_precovid)),
  nfhs4_ad_codes = c(NA, n_distinct(ad_status$nfhs4_code), n_distinct(ad_status$nfhs4_code[ad_status$in_sample]),
                     n_distinct(ad_status$nfhs4_code[ad_status$in_full_sample]),
                     n_distinct(ad_status$nfhs4_code[ad_status$in_precovid])))
print(treatment_flow)
stopifnot(treatment_flow$nfhs4_ad_codes[4] == 102, treatment_flow$nfhs4_ad_codes[5] == 40)

## (5) ADs by state: official count, NFHS-4 codes, in the full and pre-COVID samples
ads_by_state <- ad_status %>% group_by(state) %>%
  summarise(official_ads = n(), nfhs4_codes = n_distinct(nfhs4_code),
            in_full_sample = sum(in_full_sample), in_precovid = sum(in_precovid), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(official_ads))
print(ads_by_state, n = Inf)
cat("West Bengal districts flagged AD in the sample:",
    sum(kept$adp_flag[grepl("bengal", kept$state_name)]), "\n")
stopifnot(sum(kept$adp_flag[grepl("bengal", kept$state_name)]) == 0)

## (6) Treated group in every matched sample = the ADs in that sample, each with weight 1
in_full <- ad_status$nfhs4_code[ad_status$in_full_sample]; in_pc <- ad_status$nfhs4_code[ad_status$in_precovid]
for (k in names(matched)) {
  m <- matched[[k]]; ref <- if (grepl("^precovid", k)) in_pc else in_full
  t_ids <- m$dist_id[m$adp_flag == 1]
  stopifnot(all(t_ids %in% ref), all(m$weights[m$adp_flag == 1] == 1),
            grepl("full_cs", k) || setequal(t_ids, ref))   # common support may drop ADs, the others keep all
}
cat("Matched samples: treated group = ADs, weight 1, in all", length(matched), "samples\n")

write_csv(ad_status,      file.path(TABLE_DIR, "treatment_validation_ads.csv"))
write_csv(treatment_flow, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "treatment_flow.csv"))
write_csv(ads_by_state,   file.path(TABLE_DIR, "treatment_ads_by_state.csv"))
```

# Software versions

The R version and the version of every package loaded, so the results can be reproduced with the
same software. Matching results in particular depend on the versions of `MatchIt`, `optmatch`,
`Matching` and `rgenoud`.

```{r s09-session-info}
KEY_PKGS <- c("MatchIt", "optmatch", "Matching", "rgenoud", "sandwich", "lmtest",
              "dplyr", "tidyr", "readr", "haven", "ggplot2", "knitr", "rmarkdown")
versions <- tibble(package = KEY_PKGS,
                   version = vapply(KEY_PKGS, function(p)
                     if (requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) as.character(packageVersion(p)) else "not installed",
                     character(1))) %>%
  add_row(package = "R", version = paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = "."), .before = 1)
print(versions, n = Inf)
write_csv(versions, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "software_versions.csv"))
cat("Seed:", SEED, "| run finished:", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z"), "\n\n")
sessionInfo()
```
